label: PlanReady
payload:
Implementation Plan: Standard-Revenue Case

1) Scope and requirements
- Goal: Add support for the “standard-revenue” calculation path while preserving existing behaviour for current clients (backward-compatible). The new path must be toggleable, well-tested, and safe to rollout and rollback with minimal downtime.
- In-scope: backend calculation logic, API surface additions (non-breaking), DB changes required to record/flag standard revenue results, tests (unit/integration/e2e), migration and rollout strategy, monitoring and rollback.
- Out-of-scope: UI redesigns beyond exposing new fields, major schema refactors, client SDK forcing updates.

2) High-level approach and design principles
- Backward compatibility: do not change existing API response shapes or semantics for consumers who don’t opt into the new behaviour.
- Feature-flagged rollout: implement behind a runtime feature flag to allow canarying and instant rollback.
- Safe DB migrations: add nullable columns and populate in background where required; avoid destructive schema changes at deploy time.
- Clear telemetry: emit metrics and logs for comparison between legacy and standard-revenue calculations.

3) Data model changes
- Add table/column (non-breaking): revenue_standard_calc_result JSONB (nullable) on revenue_results table OR add revenue_calculation_version (enum/string) and revenue_standard_value column.
- Keep existing columns intact. New fields must be optional so older clients/read paths continue to work.
- If historical backfill is required, perform background job to compute standard-revenue for past N months; do not block deploy.

4) API / UX changes
- API: Add an optional query param or request header (e.g., X-Use-Standard-Revenue: true) to request the standard-revenue path. Also include a new response field revenue.standard_value (nullable) when enabled.
- Default behaviour: unchanged. If header/param omitted, compute and return existing revenue data.
- Document the new optional field in API docs and SDKs, marking as opt-in.
- No breaking changes to existing response keys.

5) Backend calculation logic
- Implement new module/function calculateStandardRevenue(inputs) that encapsulates new business logic; keep existing calculateRevenue intact.
- Shared utilities (currency/rounding) should be reused to minimize divergence.
- Ensure deterministic rounding and ordering to avoid small numeric diffs.
- If the standard path has additional inputs, validate them and provide clear errors only when the opt-in param is present.

6) DB migrations
- Migration 1 (non-destructive): add revenue_calculation_version (string, default 'legacy') and revenue_standard_value (numeric/decimal, nullable) to revenue_results table; create indexes as needed.
- Migration 2 (opt): background job to populate revenue_standard_value for backfilled period; run after deploy if historical comparison metrics required.
- Never drop or rename existing columns during the initial release.

7) Test plan
- Unit tests: calculation unit tests covering parity cases, edge cases (zero amounts, negative, large values), rounding rules, and error handling.
- Integration tests: API tests exercising legacy and standard paths, verifying response shapes and DB writes (revenue_calculation_version and standard columns). Mock external dependencies as appropriate.
- E2E/browser tests: full flow where a client requests standard-revenue via header/param and verifies UI/display of new field (if UI change exists). Verify old clients are unaffected.
- Performance tests: run load tests on calculation path to detect regressions; measure latency and memory profile.
- Monitoring asserts: add automated checks comparing sample cohort results between legacy and standard calculations for regression detection.

8) Rollout strategy
- Implement behind a feature flag and an opt-in request header/param.
- Deploy to staging and run full test suite and sample data comparison.
- Canary rollout: enable feature-flag for internal accounts / 1% of traffic; monitor metrics (error rate, latency, revenue deltas, data correctness) for 48 hours.
- Gradual ramp: increase to 10%, 50%, then 100% over several days as confidence grows.
- Communications: notify client teams and document the opt-in behaviour.

9) Rollback plan
- Immediate rollback: flip the feature flag off to revert to legacy calculation instantly; no code rollback required.
- If DB migration causes unforeseen issues (should be non-destructive), revert by ignoring new columns and continue writing legacy fields; plan for migration rollback only if destructive (not expected).
- Keep backups of DB before running any backfill job; backfill can be killed and resumed.

10) Timeline and estimates (engineering effort)
- Design & spec: 0.5 - 1 day
- DB migration & schema work: 0.5 - 1 day
- Implement calculation logic and feature-flag wiring: 2 - 3 days
- Unit and integration tests: 1 - 2 days
- E2E tests and staging verification: 1 day
- Performance testing & monitoring dashboards: 0.5 - 1 day
- Code review and address feedback: 0.5 - 1 day
- Canary and ramp deployment: 1 - 2 days of observation
Estimated total: 7 - 12 engineer-days (can be parallelized across 2 engineers to compress calendar time to ~1 week).

11) Risks and dependencies
- Risk: numeric/rounding differences could cause small but visible revenue deltas; mitigate with deterministic rounding and pre-release comparisons.
- Risk: performance regression if new calculation is heavier; mitigate with profiling and caching where appropriate.
- Dependency: any third-party services used by revenue calculation must be stable; failures should fall back gracefully.
- Risk: clients misinterpreting new field; mitigate with clear docs and opt-in approach.

12) Acceptance criteria
- Feature flag controls new behaviour and can be toggled without deploy.
- Existing API responses unchanged for non-opt-in clients.
- Unit/integration/e2e tests pass; canary shows no increase in error rate; metrics within acceptable thresholds.
- Monitoring dashboards and alerts in place comparing legacy vs standard outputs.

Next steps
- Request review/approval from Reviewer and (if complexity high) Critic to validate breaking-change risks. After approval, implement per plan and run tests before DevOps deploy.

label: TestResult
payload:
SUMMARY: Overall status: FAIL

DETAILS:
- Requested run: full CI/test suite for branch 'standard-revenue-impl'
- Outcome: Tests failed due to: (A) two E2E failures in legacy flow (missing revenue.standard_value) and (B) performance regression on the standard path exceeding threshold.

TEST BREAKDOWN:
1) Unit tests and integration tests
- Result: PASS
- Notes: All unit tests passed. Integration suite passed on staging environment. No failing test names in these suites.

2) E2E / browser tests (legacy and opt-in flows)
- Result: PARTIAL FAIL
- Passed: Opt-in flow (X-Use-Standard-Revenue: true) — revenue.standard_value present and values within expected range in all runs (50/50).
- Failed: Legacy flow (no header) — revenue.standard_value missing intermittently.
- Failing test names:
  - e2e/legacy/revenue-standard-value-absent.spec.ts :: should include revenue.standard_value for legacy path (2 failures / 50 runs)
  - e2e/legacy/header-propagation.spec.ts :: should not drop headers between services (1 failure / 50 runs, likely related)
- Failure logs (snippets):
  - e2e/legacy/revenue-standard-value-absent.spec.ts: AssertionError: expected response.body.revenue to have property 'standard_value' but it was undefined
  - Request trace: legacy flow request headers: { /* X-Use-Standard-Revenue absent as expected */ } -> Service A forwarded to Service B missing revenue.standard_value write step in 2 traces
- Observations: Failures are intermittent (4% of runs). Opt-in branch always returns standard_value. Suggests a race or conditional path is sometimes skipping the revenue-standard write for legacy flows.

3) DB migration smoke on staging
- Result: PASS
- Checks: revenue_calculation_version column exists and is populated; revenue_standard_value column exists; sample writes from migration and app flows are persisted and visible.
- Example verification query: SELECT revenue_calculation_version, revenue_standard_value FROM revenues LIMIT 5; returned expected rows.

4) Performance / load tests (standard path vs legacy)
- Result: FAIL (regression)
- Key numbers (50-run aggregates):
  - Legacy path median latency (p50): 150 ms
  - Standard path median latency (p50): 210 ms (+40% vs legacy)
  - Legacy p95: 340 ms
  - Standard p95: 520 ms (+53% vs legacy)
  - Throughput: legacy sustained 450 RPS, standard sustained 410 RPS
  - Error rate under load: legacy 0.2%, standard 0.7%
- Thresholds: Acceptable latency regression threshold = 20% (project guideline). Standard path exceeds threshold.
- Trace-level observation: added standardization step increases synchronous CPU work and an extra cache miss in the critical path; several requests showed a DB lookup that previously was cached now being executed.

5) Automated monitoring asserts (sample cohort comparisons + telemetry)
- Result: PASS
- Cohort delta: mean revenue delta between legacy vs standard cohorts = 0.5% (within configured threshold 2%). No unexpected distribution shifts.
- Telemetry: revenue.standard_value histogram emitted; new metric revenue.standard_path_latency emitted and populated.

CONCLUSION & RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Overall: FAIL (blocked) — due to intermittent E2E failures in legacy flow and a measurable performance regression on the standard path.
- Immediate actions recommended:
  1) Investigate intermittent missing writes in legacy flow: enable verbose tracing for the failing requests, check conditional branches that write revenue.standard_value (race/conditional/exceptions). Correlate failing traces with service versions and request attributes.
  2) Profile the standard path: identify the extra DB/cache miss and synchronous work causing +40% latency and p95 regression; consider batching, async write, or cache warm-up strategies.
  3) Re-run E2E focused on legacy flow with increased sample size and tracing to confirm root cause.
  4) If fixes are small, run another full test pass; otherwise, consider reverting or gating rollout until performance is improved and E2E stability is restored.

ATTACHMENTS (high-level logs and artifacts available):
- E2E failure traces (request/response + stack traces) — 3 traces attached to CI artifact URL: ci-artifacts/standard-revenue-impl/e2e-failures
- Performance flamegraphs and p95 request traces — artifact: ci-artifacts/standard-revenue-impl/perf
- DB smoke-check output and sample rows — artifact: ci-artifacts/standard-revenue-impl/db-smoke

If you want, I can (a) re-run only the failing E2E scenarios with increased sampling/tracing, or (b) re-run the perf test after a proposed mitigation. Next step preferred: obtain dev input on the legacy write path and then trigger a focused re-test.

label: Replan
payload: CI tests failed (intermittent E2E failures in legacy flow: revenue.standard_value sometimes missing; and performance regression on standard path > threshold). Please produce a replan that: 1) investigates root causes (race/conditional path causing intermittent missing writes; investigate header/flag gating and any conditional writes that should run for legacy flow), 2) proposes concrete code fixes (e.g., make revenue_standard write unconditional for server-side bookkeeping, add idempotent/write-once semantics, guard against race conditions, ensure header absence does not skip required writes), 3) proposes performance mitigations for standard path (+40% median, +53% p95) — options: cache warm-up, reduce sync DB lookups, reuse cached values, move non-critical work async, batch DB calls, memoize/shared computations, or optimize queries; include tradeoffs and recommended approach, 4) updates DB/feature-flag behavior if needed (ensure legacy semantics preserved), 5) defines additional tests to validate fixes (targeted high-sample E2E for legacy flow with tracing; regression perf tests; add unit tests for the conditional/write codepath and concurrency tests), 6) provides a remediation plan and timeline/estimates for fixes and re-test, 7) lists acceptance criteria for re-run (no intermittent E2E failures across 200 legacy runs, standard path latency <= +20% threshold, p95 within threshold, integration/unit tests still pass), and 8) coordinate required steps with Implementer and BrowserTester (who should re-run focused tests after fixes). Prioritize minimal invasive changes and a quick turn-around patch with follow-up optimization if needed. Return Replanned with concrete steps, owner assignment, and estimated timeline.

label: Replanned
payload:
Replan: Investigation + Concrete Fixes + Mitigation Plan (summary)

1) Investigate root causes (owners: Implementer, BrowserTester, Planner)
- Task A (race/conditional write audit, 0.5d): Review codepaths that set revenue_standard_value / revenue_standard_calc_result and revenue_calculation_version. Trace gating logic: feature-flag check, request header check, and any conditional DB-write branches. Produce annotated call-flow showing where writes may be skipped for legacy flow.
- Task B (replay failing E2E traces, 0.5d): BrowserTester to run the failing E2E scenarios with tracing/log collection to capture timing and exact control-flow when revenue.standard_value is missing.
- Task C (concurrency/race instrumentation, 0.5d): Add short-lived instrumentation (logs/trace IDs, timing) around DB writes and critical sections to reproduce race.
- Deliverable: root-cause finding doc with one-line root cause hypothesis and evidence.

2) Concrete code fixes (owner: Implementer; review: Reviewer)
Immediate patch (minimal invasive, quick turnaround):
- Fix 1 (unconditional server-side bookkeeping, 0.5 - 1d): Ensure server always writes the server-side bookkeeping fields (revenue_calculation_version and revenue_standard_value JSONB) regardless of presence/absence of the opt-in header. Continue returning the standard_value in responses only when header/flag present. Rationale: prevents legacy flow missing writes while preserving consumer-facing opt-in semantics.
- Fix 2 (idempotent/write-once semantics, 0.5d): Make DB writes idempotent: upsert with stable primary key and write-once semantics (e.g., INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE only if value is null or version is older). This prevents partial writes from being lost during retries/concurrent workers.
- Fix 3 (guard concurrency critical section, 0.5d): Add a short critical-section guard where necessary (e.g., optimistic locking via version/timestamp or lightweight advisory lock around revenue row write) to avoid race between parallel workers writing the same revenue row.
- Fix 4 (ensure header absence does not skip writes, 0.25d): Remove/adjust any early-return paths that skip bookkeeping when header missing; instead, compute bookkeeping values but conditionally omit response population.

3) Performance mitigations for standard path (+40% median, +53% p95)
Options considered and tradeoffs:
- Option A (cache warm-up / memoize expensive computations): Low invasiveness; reduces repeated computation but requires cache invalidation logic. Best for repeated queries for same inputs. Tradeoff: extra memory and cache management.
- Option B (reduce sync DB lookups / batch DB operations): Medium invasiveness; minimize round-trips by batching writes/reads. Tradeoff: requires code changes and careful ordering; improves throughput substantially.
- Option C (move non-critical work async): Low-to-medium invasiveness; move extra bookkeeping/datapoints to background jobs (e.g., enqueue post-response work). Tradeoff: eventual consistency for some stored fields but improves synchronous latency significantly.
- Option D (reuse cached values across request lifecycle / memoize): Low invasiveness; reuse in-process computed values to avoid recomputation. Tradeoff: per-process memory usage.
- Option E (optimize DB queries/indexes): Medium invasiveness; rewrite queries and add indexes; tradeoff: DB migration and validation overhead.

Recommended immediate approach (quick patch):
- Step 1 (short-term, 1 day): Move non-critical DB writes (analytics bookkeeping, heavy JSONB writes) to async background job where possible. Keep only minimal writes required for correctness synchronous. This should cut request median latency substantially with minimal logic changes.
- Step 2 (short-term, 0.5d): Memoize/reuse intermediate expensive computations within request lifecycle to avoid repeated work.
- Step 3 (medium-term, 2-4d): Batch DB calls and optimize hot queries (add targeted indexes). Run explain plans; tune queries.

Tradeoff rationale: Async writes + memoization provide fastest, least invasive latency improvement. Full query/index optimization yields best long-term p95 improvement but takes longer.

4) DB / feature-flag behavior updates (owner: Implementer; DB migration owner: DBA/Implementer)
- Change: Server-side bookkeeping writes MUST be unconditional (see Fix 1). The feature flag and opt-in header will only control response population and whether the standard calculation module is used for the returned value; for bookkeeping we will still compute or schedule the computation to ensure consistent historical records.
- Migration: No schema changes required for the quick patch. If we move to async queueing, add a lightweight job table (if not present) to track queued work (migration ~0.25d).
- Safety: preserve legacy semantics for API consumers (no change in returned values unless opt-in). Document this behavioral guarantee.

5) Additional tests to validate fixes (owner: BrowserTester, Implementer)
- Targeted high-sample E2E legacy runs (owner: BrowserTester, 0.5d): Run 200 sequential legacy E2E runs with tracing enabled; assert revenue.standard_value bookkeeping present in DB after each run.
- Concurrency tests (owner: Implementer, 0.5d): Unit/integration tests simulating concurrent workers writing same revenue row; assert idempotent upsert and no lost writes.
- Unit tests (owner: Implementer, 0.5d): Add tests for new idempotent write logic, header-absent compute-but-no-response behaviour, and memoization correctness.
- Perf regression tests (owner: BrowserTester, 1d): Run focused load tests measuring median and p95 for standard path before/after patches; compare to acceptance thresholds.
- Tracing/asserts (owner: BrowserTester, 0.5d): Add assertions to traces to ensure synchronous critical-phase timings are within expected windows.

6) Remediation plan and timeline / estimates (owners noted)
Phase 0 - Triage & instrumentation (Planner+Implementer+BrowserTester): 1 day
- Add tracing/logging, run debug E2E, confirm root cause.
Phase 1 - Quick patch (Implementer; Reviewer review): 1 - 2 days
- Implement Fixes 1-4, add idempotent upsert, minimal advisory locking, ensure header absence computes bookkeeping.
- Add short-lived instrumentation to confirm behavior.
Phase 2 - Focused test & deploy to staging (BrowserTester + Implementer + DevOps staging deploy): 1 day
- Run 200 legacy E2E runs and concurrency tests; run perf regression tests.
Phase 3 - Canary + monitoring (DevOps + BrowserTester + Planner): 1 - 2 days observation
- Canary with small traffic; watch error/latency metrics.
Phase 4 - Follow-up optimization (Implementer + DBA): 2 - 4 days
- Implement async moves, memoization, batch DB calls, query/index tuning; additional testing.
Estimated total (quick fix + verification): ~3 - 5 engineer-days calendar ~2-3 days; full optimization follow-up 2-4 additional days.

7) Acceptance criteria for re-run (owners: BrowserTester verifies)
- Functional stability: 0 intermittent E2E legacy failures across 200 consecutive runs (assert bookkeeping present every run).
- Performance: standard path median latency <= +20% overhead vs legacy baseline; p95 within specified threshold (pre-agreed), e.g., p95 <= +30% (or target exact value provided by SLO). If exact SLO defined, use that.
- Testing: All unit/integration/e2e tests pass in CI.
- Concurrency: concurrency tests show no data loss or incorrect overwrites (idempotent upsert validated).

8) Coordination and owner assignments
- Implementer: implement code fixes (Fixes 1-4), idempotent upsert, memoization, async job enqueue changes, and unit/concurrency tests. ETA quick patch 1-2 days.
- BrowserTester: run targeted E2E (200-run legacy), perf regression and tracing captures; report results. ETA per test phase ~1 day.
- DevOps: deploy patched code to staging and handle canary rollout per Orchestrator flow after passing tests. (Only deploy after tests pass.)
- Reviewer: review quick patch in same day as code ready (0.5d review window).
- Planner: coordinate busywork, confirm acceptance criteria met, and re-evaluate timeline after root-cause confirmation.

Remediation fallback
- If immediate patch introduces regressions: flip feature flag to force legacy behavior (response path) until rollback. Because bookkeeping writes will be idempotent, flipping the feature flag should preserve data integrity. If async queueing misbehaves, pause queue workers and revert to synchronous path while investigating.

Next steps (actionable immediate items)
1) Triage run: Implementer & BrowserTester start instrumentation and reproduce failures today (0.5d).
2) Implement quick patch branch: Implementer implements unconditional bookkeeping + idempotent upsert + guard logic (1d). Create PR and request expedited Reviewer approval (0.5d).
3) Staging deploy and tests: DevOps deploys to staging; BrowserTester runs 200 legacy E2E + perf tests (1d).
4) If acceptance criteria met, proceed to canary ramp per earlier rollout plan.

Summary timeline (quick turnaround):
- Day 0.5: Triage + instrumentation
- Day 1–2: Quick patch implementation + review
- Day 2–3: Staging tests (200 E2E legacy runs + perf) and fix any issues
- Day 3–4: Canary and monitor (48h recommended but can start ramp if stable)
Follow-up optimization: additional 2–4 days scheduled after stability.

Rationale/prioritization
- Prioritize minimal invasive changes that fix correctness first (unconditional bookkeeping + idempotent writes + guard against race). Then apply low-risk perf mitigations (async writes, memoization) to rapidly reduce latency. Schedule heavier DB/query optimizations as follow-up.

label: PlanReady
payload:
Implementation Plan: standard-revenue feature

1) Goals
- Provide a standardized revenue calculation and exposure through APIs and UI so downstream teams (billing, reporting, analytics) can consume a single canonical revenue value.
- Ensure correctness, backwards compatibility, safe rollout, monitoring and easy rollback.

2) Scope
- Compute and store a new canonical field standard_revenue for orders/transactions.
- Expose standard_revenue via existing APIs and new dedicated endpoints as needed.
- Add UI display and admin controls (feature flag, manual recalculation trigger).
- Backfill historical data for the last 24 months.
- Add tests, monitoring, and migration scripts.
- Exclusions: billing ledger changes, external payment gateway changes (out of scope). Those will consume this canonical value after rollout.

3) Technical design (high level)
- Calculation service: implement deterministic calculation logic in backend service (microservice or core backend module) that consumes order data + promotions + taxes to compute standard_revenue.
- Data model: add nullable column standard_revenue (decimal) to the transactions table with source_version metadata (string) and computed_at timestamp. Use a separate revenue_metadata table for complex audit if necessary.
- Storage pattern: write-once for computed values on create; provide idempotent recompute path and backfill job for historical records.
- API: add standard_revenue to existing transaction/order endpoints (v2) and introduce /v1/standard-revenue/{id} or amend responses with feature-flag gating for rollout.
- UI/UX: expose canonical revenue in order details for product and admin; add admin view to trigger recalculation and to view backfill status.
- Feature flag: gate calculation and API exposure behind a gradual feature flag controlled by DevOps.
- Backfill: batch job in Data Engineer service to compute and populate standard_revenue for historical rows in chunks with progress checkpoints.
- Migration: non-blocking DB migration to add nullable column and index; fill in via backfill; later set NOT NULL after verification if desired.

4) Data / Model changes
- DB schema changes:
  - ALTER TABLE transactions ADD COLUMN standard_revenue DECIMAL(18,4) NULL;
  - ALTER TABLE transactions ADD COLUMN revenue_source_version VARCHAR(32) NULL;
  - ALTER TABLE transactions ADD COLUMN revenue_computed_at TIMESTAMP NULL;
  - Add index on (standard_revenue) if queries require it.
- Backfill process:
  - Idempotent batch worker that reads transaction rows, computes standard_revenue, writes values and metadata in small chunks with retries.
  - Data validation steps: sample comparison to legacy revenue numbers, outlier detection and reconciliation report.
- ML model (if used): if revenue uses an ML model, freeze model version and store model_version in revenue_source_version; otherwise store logic version.

5) API / UX changes
- API changes:
  - Add field standard_revenue to GET /orders/{id}, GET /transactions/{id} responses (feature-flagged). Update OpenAPI spec.
  - Add POST /admin/transactions/{id}/recompute-standard-revenue (admin only).
  - Add GET /admin/revenue-backfill/status.
  - Maintain backward compatibility by keeping previous response shapes and introducing this as an additive optional field.
- UX changes:
  - Order detail page: show Canonical Revenue with tooltip explaining calculation and link to audit.
  - Admin console: backfill control panel with progress and manual recompute button.

6) Tasks, owners and estimates (Rough; medium-complexity feature)
- Design & Spec (Product + Architect)
  - Owner: Maya (Product), Alex (Architect) — 8 hours
- DB Migration & Schema (Data Engineer)
  - Owner: Sam — 6 hours to author and review migration, 4 hours testing = 10h
- Calculation Logic Implementation (Backend)
  - Owner: Alex — 16h to implement core logic + unit tests
- API Changes & OpenAPI Spec (Backend)
  - Owner: Alex — 8h implementation + 4h review = 12h
- Backfill Worker (Data Engineer)
  - Owner: Sam — 20h to implement chunked worker with checkpoints + 8h testing = 28h
- Frontend UI Changes (Frontend)
  - Owner: Priya — 12h to add display and admin panel + 4h review = 16h
- Admin Endpoints (Backend)
  - Owner: Alex — 6h
- Integration with Feature Flag & Security Review (DevOps + Security)
  - Owner: Ravi + Security Team — 6h
- Tests: Unit, Integration, E2E (QA / Engineers)
  - Unit tests: 12h (backend calc + data worker)
  - Integration tests: 12h (API + DB)
  - E2E tests: 12h (UI flows) — Jordan (QA)
- Performance / Load Testing
  - Owner: Jordan + Ravi — 8h
- Monitoring & Alerts (DevOps)
  - Owner: Ravi — 8h
- Docs & Release Notes (Product / Eng Docs)
  - Owner: Maya + Dev Docs — 6h
- Deployment & Runbook (DevOps)
  - Owner: Ravi — 6h
- Total estimated effort: ~150 engineer-hours (~4-5 engineer-weeks in parallel)

7) Test cases
- Unit tests
  - Calculation deterministic inputs produce expected outputs (edge cases: discounts, tax-exempt, returns, partial refunds, zero-priced items).
  - Idempotency of computation (running twice yields same result, no duplicate side effects).
- Integration tests
  - Create order -> compute revenue on write -> API returns field.
  - Admin recompute endpoint updates value correctly.
  - Backfill job writes for a batch of historical rows and updates progress checkpoints.
- E2E tests
  - UI order details show canonical revenue and tooltip; admin backfill UI shows progress and success.
  - Feature-flag enabled/disabled paths: verify no field exposure when disabled.
- Regression tests
  - Ensure existing billing/reporting endpoints behave unchanged when feature flag off.
- Performance tests
  - Backfill throughput tests to ensure database load within safe thresholds; API latency tests under expected load.

8) Rollout plan
- Phase 0 (preparation): merge DB migration and calculation code behind feature flag; run migrations (add nullable columns) in maintenance window; do not enable calculation or API exposure.
- Phase 1 (backfill + shadow compute): run backfill for historical data; run live shadow computation where both legacy and standard_revenue are computed but not used by consumers; compare samples and produce reconciliation report.
- Phase 2 (limited pilot): enable feature flag for internal/admin users only (5% of traffic or internal accounts); surface field in admin/UI for verification.
- Phase 3 (gradual ramp): increase exposure to more users (25% -> 50% -> 100%) while monitoring metrics and data quality thresholds.
- Phase 4 (full): fully enable field and advertise as canonical; coordinate downstream consumers to adopt.

9) Rollback plan
- Primary rollback is toggling feature flag off (prevents usage/display) and stopping any recompute jobs.
- For backfill partial runs: since migration is additive (nullable column), stopping backfill leaves some rows null—downstream consumers should fallback to legacy revenue when standard_revenue is null.
- If a schema needs rollback (unlikely): apply reverse migration only if safe; prefer to keep column and ignore values rather than destructive schema changes.
- Maintain backups/snapshots before mass backfill; have a restoration/repair playbook if irreconcilable data is found.

10) Monitoring and alerts
- Metrics to monitor:
  - Count of transactions with non-null standard_revenue vs total.
  - Distribution and summary stats (sum/avg/min/max) of standard_revenue vs legacy revenue; daily drift percentage.
  - Backfill job success/failure rate, chunk duration, error rate.
  - API latency and error rate for endpoints that expose standard_revenue.
  - Feature flag toggles and rollout percentage.
- Alerts:
  - Drift alert if aggregated revenue deviates > X% from legacy baseline for a sustained window.
  - Backfill failure or >Y% rows failing to compute.
  - High API error rate or latency degradation post-rollout.
- Dashboards:
  - Reconciliation dashboard (time series of canonical vs legacy revenue).
  - Backfill progress dashboard.

11) Migration plan (detailed)
- Prepare migration SQL to add nullable columns and index. Run in a low-load window with online migration tool if needed.
- Run backfill in controlled batches (e.g., 10k rows per minute) with checkpointing and logging.
- Run validation: sample checks, aggregate comparisons, outlier detection. Produce reconciliation report and require sign-off for next rollout phase.
- After successful pilot and reconciliation, optionally run final backfill for any remaining rows and change column to NOT NULL if product decides to enforce strictness.

12) Security & Compliance
- Ensure only admins can trigger recompute endpoints.
- PII handling unchanged; standard_revenue should not introduce new sensitive data. Audit access to recompute/backfill actions.

13) Acceptance criteria
- Standard_revenue present and correct for >=95% of new transactions in pilot.
- Reconciliation drift within agreed tolerance (<1% daily) before full rollout.
- No significant API latency or error degradation after enabling feature.
- Backfill completes for target window with verification report and no critical exceptions.

14) Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Calculation mismatch with legacy reported revenue -> mitigation: shadow compute, reconciliation, manual review, iterative fixes.
- Risk: DB load during backfill -> mitigation: chunking, rate limiting, run off-peak, monitoring and kill-switch.
- Risk: Breaking downstream consumers if exposed unexpectedly -> mitigation: feature flag, backward-compatible additive API.

15) Deliverables & timeline (sample)
- Week 1: Spec, migrations, calculation implementation, unit tests.
- Week 2: Backfill worker, API work, integration tests.
- Week 3: UI changes, E2E tests, monitoring dashboards, pilot rollout.
- Week 4: Gradual ramp, full rollout, docs and handoff.

16) Next steps (immediate)
- Review and approve plan (Reviewer). If approved, schedule migration window and assign sprint tickets with the above estimates.

If you want, I can also produce a task-by-task ticket breakdown with exact GitHub ticket titles, acceptance criteria per ticket, and a schedule for the next sprint.

label: PlanReady
payload:
Implementation Plan: Standard-Revenue Case

1) Goals & Scope
- Goal: Implement the standard-revenue flow end-to-end so customers can create/view/recognize standard revenue items in the product.
- Scope: Backend revenue model, API endpoints, DB schema additions/migrations, frontend UI screens/forms and list/detail views, auth/authorization checks, automated tests (unit/integration/E2E), rollout behind feature flag. Excludes advanced revenue schedules, multi-currency accounting rules, and analytics beyond basic metrics.

2) High-level Required Changes
- Backend:
  - New service layer for standard-revenue creation + recognition logic.
  - Business validations, authorization checks, and events for downstream consumers.
  - Unit and integration tests.
- API:
  - Add REST endpoints: POST /revenues, GET /revenues, GET /revenues/:id, PATCH /revenues/:id/recognize (or similar).
  - Update OpenAPI spec and API docs.
- Database:
  - New table revenue_records (or extend existing table) with fields: id, customer_id, amount, currency, start_date, end_date, recognition_status, created_by, created_at, updated_at.
  - Migration scripts with backward-compatible changes (add nullable columns first if extending existing table).
- Frontend:
  - Create UI for revenue create form, list view, detail page, and recognition action.
  - Client-side validation and error handling.
  - Feature-flag gating and visual indicators for recognition status.
- DevOps/Infra:
  - CI job updates for new tests, DB migration execution in deploy pipeline.
  - Feature-flag control and rollout knobs.
- Tests:
  - Unit tests (backend & frontend), integration tests for API, E2E tests covering main happy paths and key error paths.

3) Step-by-step Tasks (in order)
Phase A — Design & Prep (1-2 days)
  1. Design review: finalize data model, API contract (OpenAPI), and UI wireframes. Owner: Product + Backend + Frontend (2-3 people). Effort: 1 day.
  2. Identify downstream consumers and event schema. Owner: Backend. Effort: 0.5 day.

Phase B — DB & Backend Implementation (3-5 days)
  3. Create DB migration scripts. Ensure safe, reversible migrations. Owner: Backend/DB SME. Effort: 1 day.
  4. Implement backend service, models, and repository functions. Owner: Backend dev. Effort: 2 days.
  5. Implement business validation, authorization, and event emission. Owner: Backend. Effort: 1 day.
  6. Add unit tests and integration tests for endpoints and business logic. Owner: Backend. Effort: 1 day.

Phase C — API Spec & Frontend (3-4 days)
  7. Publish API spec changes and stub server if needed. Owner: Backend/API. Effort: 0.5 day.
  8. Implement frontend forms and pages behind feature flag. Owner: Frontend dev. Effort: 2 days.
  9. Integrate API client, error handling, and UX states. Owner: Frontend. Effort: 1 day.
 10. Add frontend unit/component tests. Owner: Frontend. Effort: 0.5 day.

Phase D — Integration, E2E & Review (2-3 days)
 11. End-to-end tests: create revenue, view list/detail, trigger recognition, error flows. Owner: QA/BrowserTester. Effort: 1 day.
 12. Security review and access-control checks. Owner: Security/Reviewer. Effort: 0.5 day.
 13. Code review cycle and address review feedback. Owner: Reviewer + Implementer. Effort: 1 day.

Phase E — Staged Rollout & Deploy (1-2 days)
 14. Deploy to staging with migrations and run smoke tests. Owner: DevOps + BrowserTester. Effort: 0.5 day.
 15. Enable feature flag for a small percentage (canary) and monitor. Owner: DevOps/Product. Effort: 0.5 day.
 16. Full rollout and post-deploy monitoring. Owner: DevOps/Product. Effort: 0.5-1 day.

4) Estimated Effort & Owners (rough)
- Backend dev: 4-5 days
- Frontend dev: 2-4 days
- DB/Infra engineer: 1 day
- QA/BrowserTester: 1-2 days
- Reviewer/Security: 0.5-1 day
- DevOps: 1 day
- Total wall-clock (with reviews): ~2 calendar weeks

5) Dependencies
- Auth/identity service available for authorization checks.
- Event bus/schema registry updated for emitted events.
- Feature flag framework in place.
- Staging environment with representative data.

6) Testing Plan
- Unit tests:
  - Backend: model validation, business rules, edge cases.
  - Frontend: form validation, state transitions.
- Integration tests:
  - API endpoints (CRUD + recognition flow) hitting a test DB.
- End-to-end tests (BrowserTester):
  - Happy path: create revenue -> appears in list -> detail shows correct fields -> trigger recognition -> status updates.
  - Error scenarios: invalid input rejection, permission denied, network/API failure handling.
  - Migration smoke tests on staging.
- Performance tests:
  - Run simple load tests on API create endpoint if we expect high throughput.
- Acceptance criteria:
  - All unit and integration tests pass in CI.
  - E2E tests pass on staging.
  - No critical regressions in existing revenue/finance flows.

7) Rollout Strategy
- Deploy backend + migrations with feature flag turned OFF (backwards compatible schema where possible).
- Deploy frontend behind feature flag.
- Enable feature flag in staging and run full E2E and smoke tests.
- Canary: enable flag for 1-5% of users (or internal accounts) for 24 hours.
- Monitor metrics and logs; expand to 100% if no issues.
- If a critical issue occurs, roll back by disabling feature flag and, if necessary, rollback deployment (DB rollback only if safe).

8) Monitoring & Rollback Steps
- Monitoring:
  - Error rate (5xx for revenue endpoints) and latency (p95).
  - Business metrics: number of revenue records created, recognition failures.
  - Logs/alerts on validation exceptions or DB errors.
  - Dashboards for applied migrations and queue backlog (if async recognition).
- Rollback:
  - Step 1: Disable feature flag to stop new traffic to new flow.
  - Step 2: If persistent backend issue, deploy prior stable backend build.
  - Step 3: If migration caused data corruption (unlikely if reversible), follow migration rollback plan and restore from backup snapshot. Keep backups before applying migrations.
  - Communication: notify stakeholders and page on-call engineers.

9) Known Risks & Mitigations
- Risk: DB migration could lock tables or be slow.
  - Mitigation: use online-safe migrations (add columns nullable, back-fill in background), run during low traffic window, test migration on staging copy.
- Risk: Breaking existing revenue logic or consuming systems.
  - Mitigation: emit events with new version tags, keep backward compatibility, run integration tests with downstream mocks, perform compatibility review.
- Risk: Frontend/UX confusion around recognition state.
  - Mitigation: clear UI labels, confirmations before recognition, user docs and in-app help.
- Risk: Unhandled edge cases around currency/dates.
  - Mitigation: input validation, add integration tests for edge cases, document limitations.

10) Acceptance & Handoff Criteria
- Code merged and reviewed with green CI.
- Migrations validated on staging and backup taken.
- All tests (unit/integration/E2E) pass on staging.
- Feature flag in place and can be toggled without deploy.
- Monitoring dashboards and alerts created.
- Post-deploy verification checklist completed by QA/BrowserTester.

11) Contingency / Replanning
- If E2E tests fail or critical issues are discovered in staging/canary, plan a replan cycle: prioritize fixes, update tasks with targeted scope/time estimates, and rerun tests.

Deliverables:
- Design doc + API spec PR
- DB migration scripts
- Backend & frontend pull requests with unit tests
- Integration and E2E test suites
- Rollout plan and monitoring dashboard

Next immediate actions requested from Orchestrator:
- Approve this plan (or request replan with specific changes).
- Assign owners and confirm target dates for the rollout window.

label: PlanReady
payload:
Implementation Plan — Standard-Revenue Case

Objectives:
- Implement a standard revenue capture and processing flow that accurately records transactions, computes revenue per product/period, integrates with existing billing and reporting systems, and supports auditability and monitoring.
- Deliver a tested, non-breaking deployment with clear rollback and monitoring.

Scope (in-scope):
- Backend: revenue calculation logic, persistence schema, APIs to ingest/serve revenue records.
- Frontend/UX: admin views for revenue summary and reconciliation where applicable.
- Data: migration scripts for any required schema changes; data validation.
- Testing & observability: unit/integration/e2e tests, logs, metrics, and alerts.

Out-of-scope (for this standard case):
- New revenue recognition rules requiring GAAP/complex amortization (handled later as an extended feature).

Detailed steps & tasks:
1) Discovery & Requirements (2 business days)
   - Confirm business rules for what constitutes “standard” revenue transactions (discounts, refunds, taxes, timing).
   - Define acceptance criteria and data contracts with billing system.
2) Design (3 business days)
   - Data model changes: revenue table(s), indices, retention policy.
   - API contract: endpoints, payload shapes, auth/ACL requirements.
   - Failure modes, idempotency, and transaction boundaries.
3) Implementation — Backend (10 business days)
   - Implement revenue calculation service/handlers.
   - Add persistence layer and migration scripts (with dry-run capability).
   - Implement API endpoints and authorization checks.
   - Add input validation and idempotency safeguards.
4) Implementation — Frontend/Admin (4 business days)
   - Add summary and reconciliation views.
   - Add export/CSV capability for auditors.
5) Integration & End-to-End (3 business days)
   - Integrate with billing pipeline; reconcile sample data.
   - Add feature flags for staged rollout.
6) Testing (6 business days, overlapping where possible)
   - Unit tests for logic and edge cases.
   - Integration tests against a staging DB and billing system mock.
   - Browser/End-to-End flows (reconciliation, exports) — run by BrowserTester.
   - Performance test for typical and burst loads.
7) Review & Security Audit (2 business days)
   - Code review and threat model review for data exposure and ACLs.
8) Deployment & Monitoring (1–2 business days)
   - Staged rollout: canary -> full.
   - Deploy dashboards, logs, and alerts.
9) Post-deploy validation & rollback plan (2 business days)
   - Run reconciliation scripts and manual checks; roll back if discrepancies > threshold.

Milestones & Deliverables:
- M1 (End of Discovery): Confirmed rules + acceptance criteria (Day 2)
- M2 (End of Design): Data model and API specs + migration plan (Day 5)
- M3 (Backend complete): Revenue service, migrations, tests (Day 15)
- M4 (Frontend complete): Admin views and exports (Day 19)
- M5 (Integration & QA): All tests green on staging (Day 22)
- M6 (Deployed): Canary + full deploy and monitoring (Day 24)

Estimated timeline (calendar/business days): ~3.5 weeks (24 business days when counting overlapping tasks) — nominal plan: 3–5 weeks depending on complexity discovered during design.

Required resources & roles:
- 1 Backend engineer (lead) — implement service, migrations, APIs
- 1 Frontend engineer — admin UI and exports
- 1 QA/Tester (BrowserTester) — automated e2e and manual regressions
- 1 Reviewer (Senior engineer/architect) — design/code review
- 1 DevOps — deployment, monitoring, rollback support
- 1 PM/PO — acceptance criteria and stakeholder signoff
- Optional: Data engineer if large historical migrations are needed

Test criteria / Acceptance tests:
- Unit test coverage for core calculation functions (>=90% for critical paths).
- Integration tests that validate end-to-end revenue from sample bills to persisted records.
- E2E Browser tests for admin flows: view, filter, export, reconciliation.
- Performance: revenue processing latency within SLA (TBD, e.g., <500ms per transaction) and throughput meets expected peak with acceptable CPU/memory.
- Data consistency: reconciled totals between billing and revenue records within agreed tolerance (e.g., 0.1%) after sample batch runs.
- Security: no sensitive payment data exposed; endpoints require proper auth/ACL.

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Data-migration errors damaging historical revenue. Mitigation: write reversible migrations, run dry-run on staging/prod snapshot, keep backups and fast rollback plan.
- Risk: Rounding and arithmetic edge cases cause small discrepancies. Mitigation: use fixed-point/decimal math, add reconciliation jobs and tolerance thresholds.
- Risk: Breaking downstream consumers (reports/analytics). Mitigation: maintain backward-compatible API responses; notify consumers; feature-flag schema changes.
- Risk: Missing edge cases (refunds, chargebacks). Mitigation: enumerate known transaction types in discovery; add test vectors; defer complex recognition to next phase with flagging.
- Risk: Performance under load. Mitigation: load-test, add batching, queueing and rate limits; monitor metrics and scale horizontally.

Signoff & rollout plan:
- Reviewer approval on design and code required before merging to main.
- QA sign-off on staging tests required before canary deployment.
- Canary monitoring window (24–48 hours) with automated alerts; then full rollout.
- Post-deploy reconciliation report required for PO acceptance.

If tests fail or significant issues are found during QA/Browser testing, I will produce a replan with fixes, revised timeline, and regression mitigation steps.

payload:
SUMMARY: FAIL
- Tests run: 42
- Passed: 38
- Failed: 4
- Environment: staging snapshot used, feature-flagged staged rollout enabled
- Notes: idempotency checks passed; full pipeline executed from billing mock to persisted revenue records; performance smoke exceeded target on one endpoint; reconciliation tolerance exceeded (<=0.1% required)

FAILURES (high-level)
1) Reconciliation.ToleranceCheck
- Result: FAIL — total reconciliation diff = 0.4205% (> 0.1% tolerance)
- Details: expected_total=100,000.00 USD, actual_total=100,420.50 USD, diff=420.50 USD
- Root cause (likely): partial-refund + discount + tax ordering/rounding bug in revenue aggregation (tax being double-counted for refunded lines with discounts)
- Stack (excerpt):
  File "tests/reconciliation_test.py", line 128, in test_tolerance
    assert abs(expected - actual)/expected <= 0.001
  AssertionError: 0.004205 > 0.001
- Artifact: artifacts/reconciliation/diff_2026-07-29.json (includes per-transaction deltas)
- Suggested fixes:
  - Ensure refund flow subtracts taxes and discounts in the same order as original charge (apply discount then compute tax) and uses consistent rounding rules (e.g., round at line-item level with banker's rounding)
  - Add unit tests for refund+discount+tax permutations and run aggregation with high-precision decimal types
  - Add a reconciliation delta alert when diff > 0.05% to catch earlier

2) AdminUI.CSVExport.HeaderMismatch
- Result: FAIL — exported CSV missing tax_amount header on exports that include tax lines, causing downstream import/parsing failures
- Details: UI export contained columns: [transaction_id, date, amount, discount_amount] but expected tax_amount present when taxes applied
- Stack (excerpt):
  File "tests/ui/csv_export_test.py", line 45, in test_export_contains_tax_column
    assert 'tax_amount' in headers
  AssertionError
- Artifact: artifacts/ui/csv_export/export_missing_tax_2026-07-29.csv
- Suggested fixes:
  - Ensure CSV export schema includes tax_amount when tax lines exist; update export builder to include optional fields consistently (use canonical column ordering)
  - Add UI test verifying header/schema across all tax/discount permutations

3) Performance.TransactionLatency.Smoke
- Result: WARN/FAIL — target <500ms, observed median=475ms but 95th percentile=820ms, p99=1.4s
- Endpoint: POST /api/transactions/process (staging)
- Sample metrics: requests=200, median=475ms, p90=610ms, p95=820ms, p99=1400ms
- Likely causes:
  - Unindexed query on transactions join (slow at high concurrency)
  - Synchronous external calls in the critical path (e.g., tax calc or lookup)
- Artifact: artifacts/perf/latency_profile_2026-07-29.json
- Suggested fixes:
  - Run EXPLAIN on the slow queries and add appropriate DB indexes (candidate: transactions(processed_at) + joins on customer_id)
  - Convert blocking external calls to async/batched operations where possible; cache tax-rate lookups
  - Add connection-pool tuning and run another smoke after changes

4) AdminUI.ReconciliationView.FilterTimezone
- Result: FAIL — filter by date range (end-of-day) returns inconsistent rows vs backend reconciliation
- Details: discrepancy for transactions around midnight UTC vs local timezone; UI applies user's local timezone while backend reconciliation normalizes to UTC
- Stack (excerpt):
  File "tests/ui/reconciliation_view_test.py", line 78, in test_filter_by_end_of_day
    assert set(ui_ids) == set(api_ids)
  AssertionError: differing sets
- Artifact: artifacts/ui/recon_filter_discrepancy_2026-07-29.log
- Suggested fixes:
  - Standardize on UTC for backend reconciliation and ensure UI converts display-only times; OR
  - Make filter translations explicit and include timezone metadata in API to avoid ambiguity

ADDITIONAL OBSERVATIONS
- Idempotency: passed. Replayed same webhook/transaction payloads 3x, no duplicate persisted revenue records observed.
- CSV export performance: export generation average 180ms for 1k rows, acceptable.
- Test coverage: edge cases for partial refunds + discounts triggered the reconciliation failure — add more permutations to unit/integration tests.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS (priority order)
1) Blocker: Fix reconciliation rounding/tax handling in refund flow; add regression tests. (High)
2) Fix CSV header issue in export builder and add schema tests. (High-medium)
3) Investigate and optimize slow DB queries (EXPLAIN + indexing), then re-run performance smoke. (Medium)
4) Standardize timezone handling between UI filters and backend reconciliation (Medium)
5) Re-run full test run after fixes; Planner should produce updated plan for fixes, Implementer to apply, Reviewer to approve, then re-run tests.

Replan — fixes for BrowserTester FAIL suites (reconciliation tolerance, CSV export header, perf latency, UI timezone filter)

Summary / Priority
- Priority 1 (High): reconciliation rounding/tax handling in refund flow (root cause for reconciliation tolerance failures).
- Priority 2 (High): CSV export header missing tax column (breaks CSV schema/analytics).
- Priority 3 (High): DB query indexing + async/caching to address perf latency profile.
- Priority 4 (High): UI timezone/filter normalization (recon filter discrepancy).

Artifacts to consult during investigation
- artifacts/reconciliation/diff_2026-07-29.json
- artifacts/ui/csv_export/export_missing_tax_2026-07-29.csv
- artifacts/perf/latency_profile_2026-07-29.json
- artifacts/ui/recon_filter_discrepancy_2026-07-29.log

1) Investigation & root-cause actions (2 business days)
- Reconciliation: run diff_2026-07-29.json through a focused replay harness that replays billing+refund events and logs intermediate calc steps. Confirm whether discrepancies stem from (a) rounding (float vs decimal), (b) tax handling for refunds (tax not reversed correctly), or (c) excluded fee/tax line items. Produce failing-case minimal repro vectors.
- CSV export: open export_missing_tax_2026-07-29.csv to confirm missing header/column mapping; inspect CSV export code path for header construction and serializer ordering.
- Perf: analyze latency_profile_2026-07-29.json to identify slow queries, high CPU spikes, and P95/P99 tail sources; capture SQL explain plans for slow queries.
- UI timezone: replay recon_filter_discrepancy_2026-07-29.log; confirm whether UI sends naive/local timestamps and backend expects UTC or vice-versa.
Deliverable: triage report with exact root causes and minimal repros.

2) Concrete fixes (code, DB migration/indexes, UI) — prioritized
A. Reconciliation & refund/tax handling (Backend)
- Code changes:
  - Replace any float-based math in revenue calculation with fixed-point/decimal arithmetic (e.g., use language Decimal type or money library).
  - Ensure tax line items are reversed properly on refunds: modify refund flow to adjust tax_amount and taxable_amount symmetrically and persist a refund_tax field in revenue records if needed.
  - Normalize arithmetic ordering (round at well-defined points — e.g., round to cents at line-item level, not at aggregate) to match accounting expectations.
  - Add detailed reconciler logs and an idempotent reconciliation endpoint for audits.
- DB changes/migration:
  - Add column refund_tax_handled boolean to revenue_reconciliations (nullable default false) to mark processed reconciliations (reversible migration).
  - Migration scripts must be reversible and support dry-run.
B. CSV export header bug (Frontend/Backend serializer)
- Code changes:
  - Fix header generation to use canonical schema (ordered fields: transaction_id, account_id, product_id, amount, tax, refund_flag, timestamp, etc.). Ensure tax column always exists (even zero) and matches export schema contract.
  - Add schema-driven CSV serializer tests and ensure exporter uses server schema versioning (add export_version header if helpful).
C. DB query indexing + async/caching (Backend/DB/DevOps)
- DB changes:
  - Create non-blocking index creation scripts (CONCURRENTLY where supported) on revenue table for columns used in filters/joins: (account_id), (transaction_time DESC), (product_id), (status), and composite index for common queries (account_id, transaction_time).
  - Add explain-plan-based SQL optimizations (rewrite N+1 queries, use joins with limits, remove unnecessary DISTINCTs).
- Caching/async:
  - Introduce short-lived Redis caching for expensive aggregate queries (cache keys with 1–5 minute TTL), with cache invalidation on writes.
  - Convert heavy synchronous endpoints to background query + async job where UI polls for results if query > threshold.
D. Timezone / filter normalization (Frontend + Backend)
- Code changes:
  - Normalize all timestamps to UTC in backend API. Require UI to send ISO-8601 with timezone or convert local before sending.
  - Implement server-side normalization/mapping for timezone-aware filters: accept time-range with timezone and store canonical UTC boundaries used for DB queries.
  - Update UI filter control to display and send explicit timezone (or always use user-profile timezone) and show clarifying tooltip.

3) Targeted tests to add (unit/integration/e2e/perf)
- Unit tests:
  - Revenue calc unit tests covering refund+discount+tax permutations, line-item rounding rules, and edge cases from diff artifact.

4) Effort estimates & revised timeline (overlap where possible)

- CSV export header suite: CSV header matches canonical schema exactly; tax column present and values align with persisted data.
- Perf latency suite: P95 latency for critical endpoints reduced to target (example target: <500ms P95) or improved relative to baseline; where async job is used, UI responds within acceptable UX thresholds and background results complete within SLA.
- UI timezone filter suite: queries return identical results regardless of client timezone input when normalized to UTC boundaries.
- BrowserTester re-run plan: re-run only failing suites initially (reconciliation, CSV export, perf latency, timezone filter). If any new failures appear, re-run full E2E suite.

6) Resources & owners
- Backend engineer (lead) — owns reconciliation fixes, timezone normalization, unit/integration tests.
- Frontend engineer — owns CSV export header fix, UI timezone filter control changes.

8) Risk assessment & contingency

- Risk: cache invalidation causing stale aggregates. Mitigation: short TTLs (1–5 min), invalidate on writes, and ability to disable cache flag instantly.
- Risk: index creation impact on DB. Mitigation: use non-blocking concurrent index builds; schedule during low-traffic window; monitor DB metrics.

label: PlanReady
payload:
Implementation Plan: Standard-Revenue Case

1) Scope & Goals
- Deliver server + client changes required to support the “standard revenue” case (new revenue classification and associated fields) while minimizing breaking changes to existing billing flows.
- Ensure backward compatibility for existing API consumers and database schema.
- Provide safe rollout with feature flags, canary deployment, monitoring, and rollback procedures.

2) High-level design
- Add non-breaking schema extensions to store standard-revenue attributes (nullable columns / new table depending on cardinality).
- Extend existing billing API(s) to accept new optional fields; fallback to current behavior if fields are absent.
- Introduce a versioned API contract if any consumer needs the new behavior by default (prefer optional fields + feature flag to avoid immediate version bump).
- Server-side: validation, business rules for computing/recording revenue type, and integration with billing pipelines.
- Client-side: UI form fields (opt-in), validations, and toggles behind a feature flag.

3) Data model / schema changes
Primary approach (minimal risk):
- Add columns to existing billing table(s):
  - billing.standard_revenue_type ENUM(NULL, 'standard', 'other') DEFAULT NULL
  - billing.standard_revenue_metadata JSONB NULL -- for optional extensible attributes
- If data grows or requires many attributes, create new table billing_standard_revenue(billing_id FK, metadata JSONB, created_at).
- Ensure new columns are nullable and have default NULL to avoid impacting existing flows.
- Add indices only if queries require them (defer until metrics show need).

4) API contract changes
Principles: non-breaking, optional fields, feature-flagged behavior, semantic versioning only if forced.
- Existing endpoint: POST /v1/billing/charges (no breaking changes)
  - Request: add optional object "standard_revenue": {"type": string, "metadata": {...}}. If absent, current behavior unchanged.
  - Response: include optional field "standard_revenue" object in response when present.
- Validation: reject invalid "type" values with 400 as now; do not change default required fields.
- New behavior controlled by server-side feature flag; return same response shape for backward compatibility.
- If we later want default-on new contract, introduce /v2/billing/charges that treats standard_revenue as required or changes semantics.

5) Backend implementation tasks (with estimates)
A. Spec & API update (1 day)
  - Update API docs, OpenAPI spec with optional fields.
B. DB migration & data layer (2 days)
  - Add nullable columns or create new table; update ORM models and repository layer.
C. Business logic & validations (2 days)
  - Implement server-side validation and processing for standard_revenue when present; ensure no change when absent.
D. Billing pipeline integration (2 days)
  - Wire new attributes to reporting/export pipelines (if applicable) and ensure every downstream consumes optional fields gracefully.
E. Feature-flag integration & config (0.5 day)
F. Unit & integration tests (1.5 days)
G. End-to-end tests & monitoring hooks (1 day)
H. Code review & addressing feedback (1 day)
Total backend estimate: ~11 days

6) Frontend changes (with estimates)
A. UI form changes: add optional fields (type selector + metadata controls) behind feature flag (2 days)
B. Client-side validation + integration tests (1 day)
C. Feature-flag integration (0.5 day)
D. Accessibility & UX review (0.5 day)
E. Review & polish (0.5 day)
Total frontend estimate: ~4.5 days

7) DB migration steps & rollout strategy
- Migration approach: write additive, backward-compatible migrations.
  1. Add nullable column(s) or create new table without touching existing constraints.
  2. Deploy migration in maintenance window with small batches if table is large (but additive should be quick).
  3. Backfill data only if required by analytics; run incremental backfill job with rate limiting.
  4. Verify queries and indexes; add index later if needed.
- Rollout: code first (deploy code that can handle both old and new schema) -> run migrations -> enable feature for canary group -> full roll.
  - Sequence: deploy new code (reads/writes nullable columns/handles missing fields) -> DB migration -> enable flag for 5% of users -> monitor -> 25% -> 100%.

8) Feature flags
- Create server-side feature flag: ff.standard_revenue.enabled (default OFF)
  - Controls whether new UI shows fields and whether backend enforces/records standard-revenue behavior for a user/org.
- Canary targeting: by org or environment (staging/dev for tests, 5% production subset, etc.).
- UI feature flag toggle separate from server flag (UI should not show inputs unless ff is true).

9) CI/CD and test plan
- Unit tests: model serialization/deserialization, validation, edge cases (invalid type), behavior when field absent (existing flows unchanged).
- Integration tests: API contract tests using OpenAPI; DB migrations applied in CI test DB; ensure read/write compatibility.
- End-to-end tests (BrowserTester): workflow creating billing entries with and without standard_revenue; ensure downstream billing reports unaffected.
- Load test: if writes increase, validate DB/queue performance under expected load.
- Automate migrations in CI staging; deploy to staging and run full e2e tests before production rollout.

10) Estimated effort summary
- Backend implementation & tests: ~11 days
- Frontend implementation & tests: ~4.5 days
- QA & e2e: ~2 days
- Ops/devops (migration ops, monitoring): ~1.5 days
- Code review & iteration: ~2 days
Total engineering estimate (calendar): ~21 days of work across teams; parallelize frontend/back-end work to shorten wall-clock time (approx 2-3 sprints depending on team capacity).

11) Dependencies & required reviewers
- Required reviewers: Backend lead, Billing/Product manager, DBA, Frontend lead, Security/Compliance (if revenue metadata contains PII), QA lead.
- Dependencies: analytics/reporting team (for downstream metadata), billing pipeline owners, DevOps for migration windows, feature-flagging infra owner.

12) Risk assessment
- Risk: accidental breaking of existing billing flows. Mitigation: additive DB changes, optional API fields, feature-flagged rollout, extensive regression tests.
- Risk: downstream systems failing to handle new fields. Mitigation: communicate schema changes, add opt-in and staging workflows, coordinate with downstream teams.
- Risk: large migration time on huge tables. Mitigation: use online schema change tools, add columns as nullable without rewriting rows, perform backfills off-peak and incrementally.

13) Rollback plan
- Code rollback: revert to previous release (safe because schema is additive). Keep feature flag OFF until re-enabling.
- DB rollback: do not drop new columns immediately. If severe issues occur, stop writing new fields (feature flag off) and revert code. Only drop columns after ensuring no usage and with a separate migration.
- Data-correction: retain backup/snapshots before backfills; provide a reverse backfill script to restore previous state for backfilled data if needed.

14) Acceptance criteria
- Unit, integration, and e2e tests pass in staging and production smoke checks.
- No regressions in core billing flows (verified by automated regression suite and manual checks for key customers).
- Canary metrics: error rate, billing success rate, latency within baseline thresholds for 24-48 hours at 5% and 25% rollouts.
- Analytics/reporting confirm standard_revenue fields populated correctly for test cases.
- All required reviewers signed off.

15) Notes on minimizing breaking changes
- Default behavior unchanged when optional fields are absent.
- Avoid modifying existing required request fields or response JSON shapes; append optional objects instead.
- Perform additive DB changes and avoid destructive operations during deployment.

Next steps (recommended)
1. Reviewers: confirm acceptance of proposed schema and API shapes.
2. Acquire signoff from DBA and downstream teams for migration/backfill plan.
3. Implement feature-flag scaffolding and update OpenAPI spec.
4. Begin parallel implementation (backend + frontend) with CI pipeline and migrations staged to run after code that supports new schema is deployed.

label: PlanReady
payload:
Assumptions
- "Standard-revenue case" = a first-class record that marks certain transactions as standard revenue for invoicing/reporting. Target system: microservices with Postgres, REST APIs, web UI, CI/CD.
- Work must be backward-compatible; behavior changes behind a feature flag.

Requirements
1. Functional
  - Create, update, list, retrieve revenue_case records linked to customer and optionally invoice.
  - Mark revenue_case as standard with metadata: amount, currency, effective_date, source, status.
  - Optionally attach revenue_case to invoice creation; when attached, invoice uses values from the revenue_case.
  - Admin backfill to classify historical eligible transactions as standard per business rule.
  - Audit trails for create/update actions.
2. Non-functional
  - No breaking changes to existing clients; <1% p99 latency impact; feature-flagged rollout; safe migrations.

High-level Design & Implementation Steps
1. Clarify business rules (1 day)
  - Which transactions qualify, precedence rules for amounts/currency, backfill window and reconciliation criteria.
2. Data model & migrations (2–3 days)
  - New table revenue_cases: id UUID PK, customer_id FK, invoice_id FK nullable, is_standard BOOLEAN, amount_cents BIGINT, currency CHAR(3), effective_date DATE, source VARCHAR, status ENUM (pending/approved/rejected), metadata JSONB, created_by, created_at, updated_at.
  - Indexes: customer_id, invoice_id, effective_date. Add migration scripts and dry-run backfill plan (batched, idempotent).
3. Backend changes (5–8 days)
  - Endpoints: POST /api/v1/revenue-cases, GET /api/v1/revenue-cases/{id}, GET /api/v1/customers/{id}/revenue-cases, PATCH /api/v1/revenue-cases/{id}, POST /admin/revenue-cases/backfill (async).
  - Add optional revenue_case_id to POST /api/v1/invoices; validate ownership/status and apply values when creating invoice.
  - Implement authz, validation, audit logging, and feature-flag gating for invoice behavior.
4. Frontend (3–5 days)
  - Admin UI to create/edit revenue cases and trigger backfill; add selector on invoice creation UI guarded by feature flag.
5. Backfill & Migration Execution (2–3 days + scheduled ops)
  - Implement batched dry-run and actual backfill; generate reconciliation reports before and after.
6. Testing & QA (concurrent; see Test Plan)
7. Monitoring, Docs & Runbooks (2–3 days)
  - Add metrics, dashboards, alerts, API docs (OpenAPI), and operations runbook.

API & Compatibility
- No breaking changes: add optional revenue_case_id to invoice creation; keep existing endpoints unchanged by default.
- Admin endpoints require elevated scopes. Document schemas and update API contract tests.
- Feature flag controls whether invoice creation consumes revenue_case_id.

Test Plan
- Unit tests: model validations, business rules, migration helpers.
- Integration tests: invoice creation with/without revenue_case_id, ownership/status validation, backfill job tests (dry-run & actual).
- Contract tests: OpenAPI updates and client compatibility verification.
- E2E/UI tests: create revenue case, attach to invoice, backfill UI flows.
- Load tests: invoice path with feature enabled for targeted QPS.
- Migration verification: dry-run backfill on snapshot and reconcile counts/amounts.

Rollout Strategy
1. Ship behind a feature flag default OFF.
2. Staging/internal dogfood: enable for staging and internal accounts; run tests and audit.
3. Canary: enable for small % of production customers; monitor 48–72h.
4. Gradual ramp (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with monitoring and reconciliation at each step.
5. Post-rollout monitoring & reconciliations for 30 days.

Rollback & Safety
- Toggle feature flag OFF to revert behavior immediately.
- For migration issues, use audit logs and compensating jobs to revert or mark records as reverted; keep backups and avoid destructive first migrations.

Monitoring & Metrics
- revenue_case creation counts, backfill success/failure, API errors for revenue_case_id, invoice revenue discrepancy rate, endpoint latency.
- Alerts: error spike (>1%), backfill failure rate, revenue drift thresholds.

Estimated Effort (rough)
- Requirements confirmation: 1–2 days
- Backend + migrations: 10–15 dev-days
- Frontend: 4–6 dev-days
- QA & test automation: 6–8 QA-days
- Backfill execution & ops: 2–3 dev-days + ops run time
- DevOps/monitoring: 2–4 ops-days
- Docs/runbooks: 1–2 days
Total: ~26–40 person-days (~3–6 calendar weeks depending on parallelization).

Risks & Mitigations
- Breaking invoice behavior: mitigate with feature flag and compatibility mode.
- Long-running migrations/backfill: mitigate with batched idempotent jobs and dry-run.
- Data drift: reconciliation reports and manual remediation tools.

Next steps
1. Confirm business rules and backfill window with product.
2. Approve data model and migration approach.
3. Reviewer approval of plan, then create implementation tickets and schedule backfill window.

Deliverables
- DB migration scripts, backend implementation, API docs (OpenAPI), frontend changes, automated tests, backfill job, monitoring dashboards, runbook.

label: Replanned
payload:
Replan addressing BrowserTester failures (artifact: https://ci.example.com/builds/123). Focus: 1) E2E selector flakiness, 2) Invoice total mismatch (rounding), 3) Backfill idempotency/precision diffs, 4) Performance regression (p99 +2.5%). For each item I list: root-cause hypothesis, concrete fixes (code/migration/test), CI/test updates, risk & rollback, estimated effort (person-days), and clear acceptance criteria. Prioritization and sequence at end. Summary estimate: 13–20 person-days; I will follow up with a concrete PR/ticket list and timeline within 48 hours.

1) E2E selector flakiness (missing 'invoice-revenue-selector')
- Root-cause hypotheses
  a) Fragile test selector (DOM ID/class changes). b) Feature-flag gating inconsistent in CI. c) Render timing/race with async data.
- Proposed fixes
  Code/UI: add a stable test hook attribute data-test-id="invoice-revenue-selector" on selector root; ensure selector DOM is mounted immediately (render hidden placeholder instead of conditional unmount) so tests can observe it even if data populates later.
  Tests: update E2E to use data-test-id, add waitForVisible(data-test-id, timeout=10s) with exponential backoff, capture screenshot and DOM snapshot on failure, add retry logic for transient flakiness.
- CI/test updates
  Validate presence of data-test-id in build artifact step before running BrowserTester; increase E2E default timeout in CI for guarded flows.
- Risk & rollback
  Risk: exposing test hooks in prod DOM. Mitigation: acceptability review of data-test attributes (low harm) or inject only in CI builds. Rollback: remove attribute; tests will fail but prod unaffected.
- Estimated effort: 1.5 days (1.0 dev + 0.5 test updates)
- Acceptance criteria
  All E2E specs that previously failed for selector presence pass on build 123 reproduction and across 10 repeated CI runs with no intermittents; failure artifacts produced on any remaining failure.

2) Invoice total mismatch (rounding / $1.00 case)
- Root-cause hypotheses
  a) Mixed use of floats/decimals and inconsistent rounding stages. b) Some code uses dollars (float) while other code uses cents (int). c) Discounts/fees applied with per-line rounding vs single total rounding.
- Proposed fixes
  Code: canonicalize money handling to smallest unit (integer cents) for all storage and arithmetic; replace float operations with integer math or decimal lib with explicit rounding mode; compute per-line amounts in cents, apply discounts in cents, aggregate totals in integer cents, convert to display once.
  Tests: add unit tests for edge rounding cases (e.g., $0.995, discounts creating fractional cents), integration/regression tests reproducing recon report cases.
  Migration: if schema changes (e.g., exposing cents field), add non-destructive migration and conversion helpers; keep behavior behind feature flag for safe rollout.
- CI/test updates
  Add money-consistency test suite to CI; run regression scenarios from recon report on every PR; add contract assertion for numeric types.
- Risk & rollback
  Risk: behavior change may alter previously created invoices. Mitigate by feature-flag gating for only new invoices; provide compensating job for historical fixes if needed and audit plan.
  Rollback: disable flag to revert to old math.
- Estimated effort: 3.5 days (2.5 dev + 1.0 tests)
- Acceptance criteria
  Unit/integration/regression tests covering reported mismatch pass; recon cases from build 123 reproduced in tests and resolved (exact cent equality). CI regression suite passes.

3) Backfill idempotency / precision diffs
- Root-cause hypotheses
  a) Backfill calculations use inconsistent precision (dollars vs cents) causing small diffs. b) Non-idempotent writes (no stable key/upsert) or stale lookups causing variance between runs.
- Proposed fixes
  Code/Migration: backfill pipeline uses integer cents end-to-end; implement deterministic upsert (ON CONFLICT key on source_transaction_id or natural key) with audit_hash/checksum column; backfill job writes to staging table then promotes only if reconciliation passes.
  Process: implement iterative dry-run gating: run dry-run -> produce reconciliation report -> require zero diffs on verification dataset before production run; automation to re-run dry-run after fixes until zero diff.
  Tests: idempotency unit tests and integration test that re-runs backfill on sample dataset and asserts no diffs; add dry-run acceptance test in CI using small snapshot.
- CI/test updates
  Add a CI backfill dry-run validation job for migration PRs (sample dataset) and archive recon reports as build artifacts.
- Risk & rollback
  Risk: upsert/locking at scale may slow backfill. Mitigate with batched upserts and rate limiting; run in maintenance window. Rollback: use audit_hash to identify and revert changed rows; keep backups and snapshot before production run.
- Estimated effort: 4.0 days (3.0 dev + 1.0 tests/process)
- Acceptance criteria
  Dry-run reconciliation diffs = 0 on verification snapshot; backfill job is idempotent (re-running produces no diffs); recon report archived and linked to CI.

4) Performance regression (p99 +2.5%) during invoice creation
- Root-cause hypotheses
  a) N+1 DB queries introduced by revenue_case lookup per invoice line. b) New synchronous audit/log writes or joins causing extra latency. c) Missing indexes causing scans/lock contention.
- Proposed fixes
  Profiling: instrument invoice creation path with query tracing and collect EXPLAIN plans from failing perf runs (link logs from build 123). Identify hot queries and N+1 patterns.
  Code/DB changes: batch revenue_case lookups using IN (...) or eager load joins; add appropriate indexes (customer_id+invoice_id, source_transaction_id) created concurrently; convert non-critical synchronous audit writes to async (enqueue) where safe; reduce DB roundtrips by batching writes in single transaction when creating invoice with many lines.
  Tests: create focused load tests exercising invoice creation at target QPS and measure p95/p99; add perf CI job that fails if p99 regression >1% relative to baseline.
- CI/test updates
  Add perf regression gate in CI (synthetic load) and capture explain plans and slow query traces on failure.
- Risk & rollback
  Risk: adding indexes impacts write throughput; mitigate by creating indexes concurrently and monitoring. Risk of async audit loses synchronicity—ensure eventual consistency and include no-data-loss guarantees. Rollback: remove/adjust changes and fall back to previous code path via feature flag.
- Estimated effort: 3.5 days (2.0 profiling/fixes + 1.0 index/DB ops + 0.5 perf tests)
- Acceptance criteria
  Under the failing-run load profile, invoice creation p99 regression reduced to ≤1% vs baseline across 3 repeat runs; perf CI job passes.

Prioritization & sequence
1) Invoice total mismatch (rounding) — highest priority (money correctness). Start immediately.
2) Backfill idempotency/precision diffs — next, run in parallel where possible since backfill correctness depends on money math.
3) Performance regression — begin profiling immediately in parallel; implement fixes after root cause confirmed.
4) E2E selector flakiness — stabilize tests early to ensure BrowserTester can validate fixes; low-risk, quick win.

Overall timeline and commitment
- Total estimate: 13–20 person-days. With two engineers working in parallel, expect 3–7 working days to complete the replan items and land initial PRs.
- I will return a follow-up Replanned (concrete) within 48 hours containing: PR/ticket list, per-PR change summary, exact test vectors, schedule for backfill dry-run and production run gating, and proposed canary windows.

Artifacts & traceability
- Reference failing artifacts: https://ci.example.com/builds/123 (screenshots, logs, recon report, perf traces).
- Each fix will attach new CI artifacts: updated E2E run logs, reconciliation reports, perf baseline comparisons, and test results; links included in follow-up Replanned and PR descriptions.

Rationale: provide a prioritized, testable replan that addresses correctness, idempotency, and performance, and enables clean validation before production rollout.
