label: PlanReady
payload:
Implementation Plan: Standard-Revenue Feature

1) Summary / Goal
Add robust revenue tracking, calculation, reporting, and necessary API/UI changes so the product records revenue events, computes revenue metrics (gross, net, tax, refunds), exposes them via APIs, and provides UI reporting. Support accurate accounting, incremental migration of historical data, and safe deployment with feature flags and rollback.

2) Scope
In-scope:
- Data model for revenue events and aggregated revenue records
- Backend services: ingestion, calculation, reconciliation, APIs
- UI: basic revenue dashboard, filtering, export (CSV)
- Batch jobs: nightly reconciliation and aggregation
- Tests: unit, integration, e2e, performance, data migration validation
- Monitoring/alerts and observability for revenue pipelines

Out-of-scope:
- Complex accounting integrations (ERP) beyond a simple export API
- Tax jurisdiction calculation engines (use existing tax service where applicable)

3) High-level design / components
- DB: revenue_events table (event_id, source_id, account_id, amount_gross, currency, tax_amount, discount_amount, amount_net, event_type, status, created_at, processed_at), monthly_revenue_aggregates table
- Services: Revenue Ingest service (records events), Revenue Processor (computes net/tax/refunds, writes aggregates), Revenue API (fetch events/aggregates), Export service (CSV)
- UI: Revenue dashboard page with time filters, breakdowns, charts, export
- Jobs: nightly reconcile job that verifies totals vs transactional ledger and triggers alerts on mismatch
- Feature flag to gate new endpoints/UI and migration

4) Step-by-step tasks (phased)
Phase A — Design & Prep (2-3 days)
- Finalize schema and API contract (OpenAPI) — 1d
- Define calculation rules (gross/net/tax/discount/refund) and edge cases — 1d
- Write migration plan and backfill strategy — 0.5-1d
Deliverables: DDL scripts, API spec, calculation doc, migration plan

Phase B — Data model & infra (2-3 days)
- Implement DB migrations (reversible) and create indexes — 1d
- Provision monitoring (metrics, logs, dashboards) and feature flag — 1d
Deliverables: migration scripts, infra config, feature flag toggles

Phase C — Backend Implementation (4-6 days)
- Implement Revenue Ingest endpoints + validation — 1-2d
- Implement Processor for calculations and write to aggregates — 2d
- Implement Revenue API endpoints (query, filters, pagination) — 1-2d
- Add input validation, idempotency handling, and error paths — 0.5-1d
Deliverables: service code, API docs, unit/integration tests

Phase D — UI & Export (3-4 days)
- Implement dashboard UI (filters, charts, table) — 2d
- Implement CSV export and link to API — 1d
- Add UI feature-flag gating and user permission checks — 0.5d
Deliverables: UI pages, e2e test scripts, UX screenshots

Phase E — Batch jobs & Reconciliation (2-3 days)
- Nightly reconciliation job + discrepancy alerting — 1-2d
- Aggregation jobs for monthly totals and backfill script — 1d
Deliverables: batch job code, alerting playbook

Phase F — Testing & QA (3-5 days, parallel)
- Unit tests for calculation logic — 1d
- Integration tests for ingestion->processing->API — 1-2d
- E2E tests covering UI flows and CSV export — 1d
- Performance test for expected ingestion throughput and query latency — 1d
Deliverables: test reports, coverage metrics

Phase G — Migration, Release & Monitoring (2 days)
- Run backfill on staging, verify reconciliation — 0.5-1d
- Canary deploy with feature flag on production, monitor for anomalies — 0.5-1d
- Full rollout and disable feature flag rollback window — 0.5d
Deliverables: migration logs, canary results, monitoring dashboards

Total estimate: ~16-24 engineering days (3-5 weeks depending on parallelization and reviews)

5) Estimates (per role effort, rough)
- Backend engineer: 10-14d
- Frontend engineer: 3-4d
- DB/DevOps: 2-3d
- QA: 2-3d
- PM/Designer: 1-2d

6) Required tests
- Unit tests: calculation rules, idempotency
- Integration tests: end-to-end ingestion -> processing -> API
- E2E/UI tests: dashboard flows, exports
- Data migration tests: backfill dry-run and checksum comparisons
- Performance/load tests: ingestion throughput and aggregate query latency
- Security: authorization checks for APIs and UI

7) Rollback / Recovery strategy
- All DB migrations reversible where possible; use two-phase changes (add columns, backfill, switch reads to new columns, drop old) to avoid destructive migrations.
- Feature flag gating for API/UI and processing pipeline; keep old pipeline running until new pipeline is validated.
- Backout steps: disable feature flag, stop ingest into new tables, re-route ingestion to legacy path, run reconciliation to confirm parity, restore previous schema if needed.
- Data recovery: keep detailed migration/backfill logs and snapshot DB before full backfill when executing on prod. Use incremental backfill instead of one-shot where data size is large.

8) Dependencies & Assumptions
- Assumes existing tax calculation/third-party service for jurisdictional taxes (if not, add time to integrate/build)
- Assumes transactional source(s) expose necessary identifiers and amounts; otherwise we need adapter work
- Assumes access to DB migration tooling and capacity to run backfills outside peak hours
- Assumes feature flagging system available

9) Risks & Mitigations
- Risk: calculation mismatch with legacy accounting => mitigation: reconciliation job, parallel run and compare before cutover
- Risk: large backfill time/lockout => mitigation: incremental backfill, pagination, and snapshot testing
- Risk: performance regression on DB => mitigation: add indexes, rate-limit ingestion, run load tests

10) Acceptance criteria / Deliverables
- Revenue events recorded and queryable via API
- UI dashboard shows correct aggregates and allows export
- Nightly reconciliation job running with alerts for mismatches
- Tests passing: unit/integration/e2e with coverage >= agreed threshold
- No critical discrepancies after 2-week canary period

Next steps: review plan, approve or request changes (e.g., deeper accounting integration or specific KPI definitions).

payload:
Implementation Plan: Standard-Revenue Case

1) Scope
- In scope: implement the standard-revenue flow end-to-end including backend revenue model, APIs, DB schema updates, UI changes in billing dashboard, reporting export, unit/integration/e2e tests, docs, deployment and rollback capabilities. Include data migration for existing accounts where necessary. Validate with sample production-like data.
- Out of scope: premium/edge revenue models, marketing analytics beyond export, third-party connector modifications.

2) Objectives / Success Criteria
- Accurate revenue computation for standard cases across existing accounts.
- No regressions on non-revenue features; passes automated regression suite.
- Deployable behind a feature flag; ability to rollback within 30 minutes.

3) Detailed Tasks (with owners)
A. Analysis & Design (2 business days)
  - Review current revenue model and data (Planner/Architect).
  - Define schema changes, API contracts, and UI wireframes (Architect + Product).
B. Implementation (10 business days)
  - Backend: implement revenue calculation service, business rules, API endpoints (2 backend devs).
  - DB: add tables/columns and migration scripts; migration written to be backward-compatible and incremental (DB dev).
  - Frontend: billing dashboard changes, feature flag gating, small UX copy updates (1 frontend dev).
  - Logging/metrics: add telemetry for key revenue events (dev).
C. Testing & QA (4 business days, overlapping where possible)
  - Unit tests for all new logic (devs).
  - Integration tests for APIs and DB migrations (dev + QA).
  - E2E browser tests covering billing flows (BrowserTester/QA).
  - Performance tests for high-volume calculation scenarios (QA/DevOps).
D. Documentation & Training (1-2 days)
  - Update API docs, runbook for ops, and release notes (Tech Writer).
E. Pre-Deployment & Release (2 days)
  - Deploy to staging, run full test suite, stakeholder sign-off (DevOps + Product).
  - Schedule production deploy in low-traffic window with rollback plan ready.

4) Deliverables
- Design doc and API contract
- DB migration scripts and rollback scripts
- Backend service code and unit tests
- Frontend changes and E2E tests
- CI pipeline updates to run new tests
- Release notes, runbook, and rollback checklist

5) Timeline (approximate, total ~3 weeks calendar)
- Week 1: Analysis & Design (2 days) + begin implementation
- Week 2: Implementation (continuing) + unit/integration tests
- Week 3: Finish implementation, QA/E2E, performance tests, docs, staging deploy
- Deployment: schedule on Monday of Week 4 or earlier after sign-off
Note: parallelize tasks where possible; milestones at end of Design, Implementation, QA, and Pre-Deployment.

6) Required Resources
- 1 Planner / Product Owner (part-time)
- 1 Architect (design) (part-time)
- 2 Backend Engineers (full-time for implementation)
- 1 Frontend Engineer (full-time/part-time depending on scope)
- 1 DB Engineer (part-time for migrations)
- 1 QA Engineer / BrowserTester (full-time during QA window)
- 1 DevOps Engineer (for staging/prod deploys and performance testing)
- 1 Tech Writer (docs)
- Staging environment mirroring production (compute + test data)
- CI/CD pipeline with test runners and feature flagging system

7) Rollback Plan
- Deploy behind a feature flag; enable for 0% then canary to small cohort.
- Prior to production deploy: take DB backups + snapshot for affected tables.
- Use atomic migration pattern: deploy code that supports both old/new schema, run migration, then flip feature flag.
- Rollback steps:
  1) Immediately flip feature flag to off.
  2) If issue persists, run automated rollback job to restore DB snapshot or revert problematic migration (if irreversible, follow runbook manual steps).
  3) Redeploy previous stable service version.
- Estimated time-to-rollback (flag-only): <5 minutes; full DB restore worst-case: depends on data size (target <30–60 minutes).

8) Risk Assessment & Mitigations
- Risk: Data migration causes downtime or corruption. Mitigation: incremental, reversible migrations, pre-run on staging copy, DB backups, validation scripts.
- Risk: Revenue calculation edge-case mismatch vs. legacy system. Mitigation: side-by-side validation on a sample dataset; reconcile reports before flipping flag.
- Risk: Performance regressions under load. Mitigation: performance tests and profiling; add circuit-breakers and throttling.
- Risk: UI/UX regressions. Mitigation: feature flagging, staged rollout, user acceptance testing with product team.
- Risk: Insufficient test coverage. Mitigation: enforce CI gates, minimum coverage thresholds for changed modules.

9) Test Cases / Acceptance Tests
- Unit tests: all revenue rules, boundary and null cases, exception handling.
- Integration tests: API returns expected revenue numbers for seeded datasets; migration applied and rolled back successfully.
- E2E tests: user creates invoice/subscription -> billing dashboard shows computed revenue; exports match report values.
- Regression tests: existing unrelated billing flows unchanged.
- Performance tests: simulate X% of production traffic for revenue computation endpoints and ensure latency < SLO and no memory leaks.
- Validation step: reconcile system-calculated revenue vs. legacy reports for a statistically significant sample (e.g., top 100 accounts by volume).

10) Post-Deployment Monitoring
- Dashboards: revenue metrics, error rates, latency, migration validation metrics.
- Alerts: on revenue deviation thresholds, elevated error rates, increase in failed background jobs.
- Post-deploy smoke test checklist to run at +15m, +1h, +24h.

11) Contingencies
- If reconciliation shows >0.5% discrepancy on sampling: hold rollout and trigger incident review.
- If performance issues detected: throttle feature, roll back, and profile.

Estimated effort: ~6–8 dev-weeks across roles (parallelized); early-stage review needed after Design to confirm estimates.

Next steps: request Reviewer review/approval of design doc; schedule architecture walkthrough; allocate dev resources and staging window.

Replanned Hotfix Plan — RCA, Fixes, Tasks, Verification, Timeline, Risks

Summary
- Deliver hotfix branches addressing (A) promo NPE and DB perf for promo lookup and (B) subscription payment flakiness vs payment-sandbox. Run targeted verification (the 2 failing E2E tests + 2 perf checkpoints) on hotfix branches before continuing deployment. Recommend blocking production rollout until verification passes.

1) RCA (root-cause evidence from artifacts)
- Promo NPE (artifacts/logs/revenue-service/abc123/promo_500.log): NPE in PromoService.validatePromo when promo.metadata.rules is null; stack shows code assuming promo.rules non-null during checkout validation. Root cause: defensive validation missing and data corruption/missing metadata for a subset of promos (likely from legacy import/migration).
- Subscription payment flakiness (artifacts/logs/payment_sandbox_402.log): repeated HTTP 402 and long response latencies from payment sandbox. Observed request timeouts at client side; intermittent failures correlated with sandbox latency spikes rather than business logic. Root cause: insufficient retry/backoff and conservative client timeouts for sandbox environment; no idempotent retry handling for the verification path.
- Promo DB perf checkpoint failure (artifacts/perf/*): promo lookup queries show full-table scan patterns and high latency under load (explain plans show missing indexes / non-SARGable predicates). Hot path uses promo lookup during checkout, causing TTFB regression.

2) Proposed fixes
A. Promo NPE fixes (code + data)
  - Code fix: add defensive null-checks in PromoService.validatePromo and promo application flow; return explicit ValidationError for missing promo metadata instead of throwing NPE. Example: if (promo == null || promo.getRules() == null) throw new PromoValidationException("invalid_promo_metadata");
  - Data validation script: find promos with null/invalid metadata and mark them disabled or backfill rules where possible. SQL example: SELECT id FROM promos WHERE rules IS NULL OR rules = '';
  - Migration/data-clean options:
    - Safe path (preferred): create a one-off data-migration script that marks problematic promos as disabled and logs records to a reconciliation table for product review.
    - Aggressive path (only with product sign-off): backfill rules from audit/logs for a subset of known promo types.

payload:
Replanned Hotfix Plan (summary)

RCA
- Promo NPE: null pointer in PromoService.validatePromo when promo.metadata.rules is null (data corruption/legacy import + missing defensive checks).
- Payment flakiness: payment-sandbox high latency + 402s causing client timeouts; client lacks idempotent retry/backoff.
- Promo DB perf: promo lookup queries cause full-table scans (missing indexes / non-SARGable predicates) leading to high TTFB.

Proposed fixes
1) Promo NPE (code + data)
- Code: add defensive null-checks and explicit PromoValidationException for missing metadata; fail-safe path returns user-friendly validation error.
- Data: data-validation script to find promos with null/invalid rules; safe migration to mark them disabled and write to a reconciliation table; optional backfill only with product sign-off.
- Tests: unit tests for null/empty rules; integration test for promo validation error.

2) Payment sandbox resilience
- Code: implement idempotent retries with exponential backoff (3 attempts: 200ms -> 500ms -> 1s) for idempotent verification calls; add circuit-breaker and sandbox-specific increased timeouts (2s -> 5s) in staging config.
- Escalation: contact sandbox provider if sustained 4xx/5xx beyond transient period.
- Tests: integration tests simulating delayed sandbox responses; E2E to confirm graceful UX on payment declines.

3) Promo DB performance
- DB: add index on promos(code) and composite index on (account_id, code, active) where applicable; rewrite queries to remove leading-wildcard LIKE.
- Cache: introduce Redis cache for promo lookups (TTL 5–15m) with invalidation on updates.
- Validation: run EXPLAIN ANALYZE before/after to measure impact.
- Estimated impact: DB index expected to drop median lookup from ~150–250ms to ~10–30ms; caching yields single-digit ms for hits.

Concrete tasks, owners, effort (est.)
- Create hotfix branches & CI gating (DevOps) — 4h
- Promo NPE code + unit tests (Backend A) — 8h
- Promo integration + E2E update (Backend A + BrowserTester) — 12h
- Data validation script + safe migration (DB Eng + Backend A) — 12h
- DB index additions & query rewrites + EXPLAIN (DB Eng) — 8h
- Redis caching implementation (Backend B + DevOps) — 16h
- Payment retry/backoff + circuit-breaker (Backend B) — 12h
- Integration tests simulating sandbox delays (Backend B + QA) — 12h
- E2E/perf orchestration & perf checkpoints (QA + DevOps) — 8h
- CI gating for targeted reruns (CI Eng) — 6h
- Staging verification & triage (All) — 8h
Total ~64 engineer-hours; parallelizable to ~3 business days if staffed.

Verification plan (targeted)
- Branch: create hotfix/promo and hotfix/payment (or combined) from abc123.
- CI: run unit/integration, then only the 2 failing E2E tests (promo validation; subscription payment flow) and the 2 perf checkpoints (checkout TTFB, promo DB lookup) in staging with prod-like data.
- Acceptance criteria: both E2Es pass reliably on 3 consecutive CI runs; checkout TTFB median < configured SLO (example target <300ms, P95 <700ms); promo DB lookup median <50ms, P95 <200ms; no new regressions.
- If failures persist: iterate on hotfix branch until acceptance criteria met.

Branching & deployment advice
- Deliver as hotfix branch(es). Prefer separate PRs: code fixes first (behind feature flag), then safe data migration during maintenance window.
- Recommendation: block production deployment until targeted verification passes because these issues affect checkout and revenue-critical flows.

Updated timeline (hotfix-focused)
- Day 0: create hotfix branches, assign owners, start parallel work.
- Day 1: promo NPE code + unit tests complete; begin data validation; DB index testing on staging copy.
- Day 2: payment retry/circuit-breaker + timeouts; caching prototype; integration tests.
- Day 3: run targeted E2E + perf checkpoints, triage, iterate; upon 3 passing runs, merge and schedule prod deploy behind feature flag.
(3 business days aggressive; 5 days conservative.)

Risks & mitigations
- Data migration may disable valid promos: run dry-run on staging and produce reconciliation report; product review before mass changes.
- Index creation may affect writes: create indexes online / during low-traffic window and monitor.
- Retries could amplify load: cap retries, exponential backoff, monitor request volume.
- Caching may produce stale reads: short TTL (5–15m) + invalidation on update events.

Required resources
- Backend Dev A (promo fixes), Backend Dev B (payment + caching), DB Engineer, QA/BrowserTester, DevOps/CI Eng, Product/PM for migration decisions, Tech Writer for runbook.

Next steps
- I will create the hotfix branches, open PRs for the code fixes behind a feature flag, and coordinate assignment of owners. Requesting Reviewer quick review once PRs are ready.

payload:
Implementation Plan: standard-revenue feature

1) Scope
- Implement a canonical “standard revenue” calculation and delivery path used by billing, reporting, and analytics. This includes API endpoints, DB schema (revenue table/fields), business-logic code, configuration/feature-flag, tests, metrics, rollout and rollback procedures.
- Backwards compatibility: existing consumers should remain unaffected until feature flag fully enabled.

2) High-level approach
- Implement feature behind a feature flag (standard_revenue_v1).
- Use a backward-compatible DB migration pattern (expand schema, backfill optional column, read-path gated by feature flag). No destructive migrations in the deployment window.
- Deploy incrementally: internal QA -> canary (small % of traffic) -> full rollout.

3) Tasks, owners, and timeline (estimates assume an experienced team, 2-week sprint total)
- Day 0: Kickoff & design (Planner + Implementer + Reviewer) – 1 day
- Days 1–3: Design & API spec (Planner/Implementer) – produce API contract, data model, edge-case docs – 2 days
- Days 3–8: Implementation (Implementer)
  - Code: revenue calculation logic, API endpoints, validation – 3 days
  - DB: Add new columns/table and populate migration scripts – 2 days
  - Config: Add feature flag and config entries – 1 day
- Day 6: Internal code review (Reviewer) – 1 day (parallel with implementation)
- Day 8: Critic review (Critic) — if marked high complexity; otherwise skip – 1 day
- Days 9–10: Unit & integration tests implementation (Implementer + BrowserTester for E2E design) – 2 days
- Day 11: QA and E2E testing (BrowserTester) – 1 day
- Day 12: Performance & load testing (BrowserTester) – 1 day
- Day 13: Release candidate and pre-deploy checklist (Planner + DevOps) – 1 day
- Day 14: Canary deploy and monitoring (DevOps + BrowserTester), then progressive rollout – 1–3 days for observation

Owners
- Planner: design, rollout plan, risk assessment
- Implementer: code, migrations, tests
- Reviewer: formal code and design review approval
- Critic: deep critique if complexity flagged
- BrowserTester: E2E tests, performance tests, test reports
- DevOps: deploy and manage feature-flag rollout
- Orchestrator: coordinate and sign off each phase

4) Dependencies
- Auth service API (for revenue ownership validation)
- Billing/Payments provider API (if revenue tied to external provider)
- Analytics pipeline schema (to consume new revenue field)
- CI/CD for automated tests and rollout
- Feature flag system (supports percentage rollouts and immediate toggle)

5) Required changes (code/config/data)
- Code
  - New module or service functions: compute_standard_revenue(order/events)
  - API: /v2/revenue/standard (read and optionally re-calc endpoint)
  - Integration hooks for billing & reporting consumers
- Config
  - feature flag: standard_revenue_v1 (default OFF)
  - new config entries for thresholds and backfill controls
- Data
  - DB migration: add column revenue_standard (nullable) to orders/revenue table or new revenue_standard table
  - Backfill job: optional, run under maintenance window or as safe background process
- Tests
  - Unit tests per business rule
  - Integration tests with DB
  - E2E tests simulating real flows
  - Regression tests to ensure old paths unchanged when flag OFF

6) Test cases (minimum set)
- Unit: verify each rule, boundary values, negative/edge cases
- Integration: calculation correctness with DB save/read
- E2E: full flow: create order -> compute revenue -> store -> report consumer reads expected value
- Backfill: run backfill on sample dataset -> verify idempotency & performance
- Canary validation: run canary traffic and compare revenue totals vs baseline for discrepancies
- Non-regression: existing APIs unchanged when feature flag OFF
- Load/perf: calculation under expected peak throughput and 2x traffic

7) Rollout strategy
- Feature flag OFF in staging by default; enable in staging for QA
- Canary: enable feature flag for 1% of users (or 1 instance) for 24–72 hours, monitor metrics
- Gradual ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with observation windows and acceptance criteria at each step
- Acceptance criteria per stage: error rate <= baseline + 0.1%, revenue delta within expected tolerance, no data loss
- Full rollout when acceptance criteria met for the configured observation window

8) Rollback strategy
- Immediate: flip feature flag OFF to stop new reads/writes to new path
- If DB migration was applied and is incompatible: have a reversible migration strategy (avoid destructive changes, use dual-write or feature-guarded read path). If backfill caused incorrect data, run a corrective migration or restore from backups depending on severity.
- Re-deploy prior stable binary only if flipping flag insufficient.

9) Monitoring & metrics
- Revenue totals (new vs baseline) and percent delta
- Error rates, latency of revenue endpoints
- DB metrics: migration/backfill progress, lock times, query durations
- Alerts: abnormal delta (>X%), increase in error rate, increased latency

10) Risks & assumptions
- Assumptions: feature flag system works reliably; third-party billing APIs stable; DB can handle schema change/backfill traffic.
- Risks: calculation edge cases not covered -> revenue mis-reporting; DB migration could cause locks; incorrect backfill causing data corruption; downstream consumers failing to adopt new field.
- Mitigations: thorough review, critic for complex logic, run backfill in batches, monitor canary closely, keep old path available until stable.

11) Acceptance criteria for Done
- Automated test suite passing (unit+integration+E2E)
- Reviewer and Critic (if required) approvals
- Canary stage shows acceptable metrics
- Documentation updated (API docs, runbooks, data dictionary)
- Rollout playbook and rollback steps validated

Next steps requested of Orchestrator
- Approve plan and indicate whether to trigger Critic review (if you consider complexity high)
- Confirm timeline/priority and allocate Implementer, Reviewer, BrowserTester, DevOps resources

Planner deliverable: this plan document, migration scripts draft, API contract, and test matrix ready upon approval.

label: PlanReady
payload:
Implementation Plan: Standard-Revenue Case

1) Scope & Objectives
- Scope: Implement end-to-end support for the “standard revenue” billing scenario across backend, data model, APIs, and UI. This includes recording revenue events, computing routine revenue summaries, exposing APIs for retrieval and reporting, and ensuring accurate migrations for existing customers.
- Objectives:
  - Add data model fields and ensure data integrity for revenue items.
  - Provide backend services to create, update, and query standard revenue records.
  - Expose REST API endpoints for ingestion and reporting, with pagination, filtering, and auth.
  - Update UI (admin dashboard + reporting pages) to show standard-revenue items and summary metrics.
  - Add automated tests (unit, integration, end-to-end) and migration scripts.
  - Ensure safe deploy with rollback and monitoring.

2) Required Code / Data / Schema Changes
- Database schema changes:
  - Add table revenue_records (if not present) or add columns to existing table:
    - id (pk), account_id (fk), amount (decimal(12,2)), currency (string), revenue_type (enum: "standard", ...), recognized_at (datetime), created_at, updated_at, source_id (nullable), status (enum: pending, recognized, failed).
  - Indexes: (account_id, recognized_at), (revenue_type), (status).
  - Migration script: safe backfill for existing rows (see migration section).
- Backend service changes (microservice or monolith revenue module):
  - Domain model RevenueRecord with validation, currency handling, and business rules for "standard" revenue.
  - Business logic for create/update/recognize operations and consistent timestamping.
  - New repository/DAO methods to query by account/date/revenue_type, and for summary aggregation queries (SUM(amount) GROUP BY period).
- API layer changes:
  - POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/revenue - create revenue record (body: amount, currency, revenue_type, recognized_at optional, source_id optional).
  - GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/revenue - list with filters: date_from, date_to, revenue_type, status, page, per_page.
  - GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/revenue/summary - aggregated metrics by period (day/week/month) and currency.
  - Add OpenAPI spec entries, request/response models, and error codes (400/401/403/404/429/500).
- Frontend/UI changes:
  - Admin dashboard: new tab or card showing latest standard revenue items and quick summary metrics.
  - Reporting page: filter/visualize standard revenue over time with dropdowns for period and currency.
  - Forms: create revenue record UI (if manual entry required) with validations.
- Auth/Zoning:
  - Ensure endpoints require proper scopes (revenue:read, revenue:write) and enforcement in middleware.

3) API/UX Updates (if any)
- API:
  - Define request/response JSON examples and schema in API docs.
  - Versioning: If API is public, consider v2 or feature-flag the new endpoints. Provide compatibility notes.
- UX:
  - Add a single card on admin home with "Standard Revenue (30d)" and link to detailed report.
  - Provide CSV/Excel export for report endpoint.
  - Provide inline help tooltip explaining "standard revenue" definition and recognition rules.

4) Build & Deployment Steps
- CI pipeline changes:
  - Add new unit/integration test suites to run in CI.
  - Linting and static checks for new code.
- Build steps:
  - Backend: run unit tests, build artifact (jar/docker image), push to registry with tag = commit-sha.
  - Frontend: run unit tests, build static assets, create versioned bundle.
- Deployment strategy:
  - Deploy backend using blue-green or canary (recommended) to avoid downtime: deploy new service version to subset of instances, run smoke tests, gradually route traffic.
  - Deploy frontend as atomic asset; ensure cache invalidation for static assets.
  - Release migrations in two phases when schema changes are non-blocking: (1) deploy migration to add columns nullable and populate defaults, (2) deploy code that writes new columns, (3) optionally convert columns to non-null and enforce constraints in a subsequent migration after all writes are on new code path.
- Sequence:
  1. Merge feature branch to main (after review).
  2. Run full CI including integration & e2e tests.
  3. Create deployment artifact.
  4. Run DB migrations (backfill / non-blocking first).
  5. Deploy backend (canary) and run smoke tests.
  6. Deploy frontend.
  7. Promote backend to full traffic.

5) Test Cases
- Unit tests:
  - Model validation tests (amount rounding, currency enforcement, required fields).
  - Business logic tests for recognition flow, status transitions, and error handling.
  - Repository tests (mock DB) for queries and aggregations.
- Integration tests:
  - API endpoint tests (create, list, summary) using test database.
  - Auth tests verifying scopes and permission errors.
  - Migration tests verifying forward/backward compatibility on test fixtures.
- End-to-end tests (BrowserTester):
  - UI flow: create revenue record (if applicable) and check it appears in list and summary.
  - Reporting: filter by date/revenue type and verify aggregation matches expected values.
  - CSV export and content validation.
- Performance tests:
  - Aggregation query performance under production-like dataset (e.g., 10M records) — ensure indexes and query plan are acceptable.
- Test data:
  - Provide deterministic fixtures with multiple currencies, statuses, and dates across boundary conditions (month/year boundaries, DST, leap day).

6) Rollback & Migration Strategy
- Migration strategy (safe phased approach):
  - Phase 0 (pre-migration): Create new migration to add columns as NULLABLE and add indexes without locking long-running ops where possible.
  - Phase 1 (deploy code): Release backend that can read and write both old and new columns (feature-flagged behavior if needed).
  - Phase 2 (backfill): Run background job to backfill existing revenue data into new fields where appropriate. Monitor performance and throttle.
  - Phase 3 (constraint tighten): After backfill and stable runs, add NOT NULL constraints and drop old columns if needed.
- Rollback plan:
  - If issue during deploy: route traffic back to previous backend version (blue-green) and monitor errors.
  - If migration causes problem: reverse migration only if safe (best avoid destructive migration in first deploy). Use backups and DB snapshots before Phase 2 backfill and before Phase 3 constraints.
  - Keep feature toggles to disable new API endpoints or UI features quickly.

7) Risk Assessment & Mitigation
- Risk: Data loss or incorrect revenue recognition during migration.
  - Mitigation: Non-destructive migrations, full DB backup before migration, test on staging with production-sized data, backfill conservatively.
- Risk: Performance regression for aggregation queries.
  - Mitigation: Create proper indexes, benchmark queries on staging with representative dataset, add materialized views or pre-aggregations if needed.
- Risk: API break for external consumers.
  - Mitigation: Version APIs or feature-flag, keep backward compatibility, document changes and provide deprecation timeline.
- Risk: Bad UX or user confusion.
  - Mitigation: Add inline help, staged rollout to internal users first, collect feedback.
- Risk: Authorization/permission leaks exposing revenue data.
  - Mitigation: Audit middleware, run auth tests, ensure least-privilege scopes.

8) Time & Effort Estimates (per task) — assumptions: 2 backend devs, 1 frontend, 1 QA, 1 DevOps; medium complexity codebase
- Design & spec (including API docs): 8–12 hours (1 day)
- DB schema migration & indexing (dev + migration scripts): 12–20 hours (1.5–2.5 days)
- Backend implementation (models, business logic, API handlers, unit tests): 24–40 hours (3–5 days)
- Frontend changes (UI, reports, forms, unit tests): 16–24 hours (2–3 days)
- Integration tests & test data: 12–20 hours (1.5–2.5 days)
- End-to-end tests (automation + runs): 8–12 hours (1–1.5 days)
- Performance testing & optimizations: 8–16 hours (1–2 days)
- CI/CD pipeline updates & deployment playbook: 8–12 hours (1–1.5 days)
- Staging rollout, monitoring setup & runbook: 6–10 hours (1 day)
- Migration backfill run & supervision: 4–8 hours (0.5–1 day) + possible long-running background job time depending on dataset
- Contingency (bug fixes, review cycles): 20% of total ~ 2–4 days
- Total calendar time estimate (parallel work considered): 2–3 weeks to production depending on team availability and complexity of existing platform.

9) Acceptance Criteria
- All unit and integration tests passing in CI.
- E2E tests for UI/reporting passing in staging.
- No regression in existing revenue APIs (smoke tests pass).
- Aggregation queries meet performance SLAs in staging.
- Migration completes without data loss; sampling checks confirm correctness.
- Monitoring alerts and dashboards in place for first 72 hours after prod rollout.

10) Rollout & Post-deploy Validation
- Rollout to 10% traffic (canary) for 1–2 hours, run smoke tests and reconcile sample accounts.
- If stable, increase to 50% for 2–4 hours, then full rollout.
- Post-deploy: run reconciliation job comparing pre-deploy snapshot vs new calculations for a sample of accounts; monitor error/exception rates and latency.

11) Dependencies
- Authentication service updates (if new scopes needed).
- DB maintenance window coordination for index creation if locks expected.
- Frontend design mockups (small effort) and product sign-off.

12) Notes & Open Questions
- Do we need multi-currency conversion for summary endpoints or only per-currency aggregation?
- Is there an existing revenue table or should we create a new table? (affects migration complexity)
- Are there SLAs for reporting latency that would require pre-aggregation?

Next steps (recommended immediate actions)
1. Product/design: answer Open Questions and sign off on API contract and UI mockups (1 day).
2. Team kickoff: assign backend/frontend/migrations and schedule migration window (30–60 min meeting).
3. Implement incrementally following the sequence above, starting with DB migration (nullable) and API skeleton.

Estimated total engineering effort: ~ 8–12 engineer-days of focused work (excluding long-running backfill and contingency), calendar time ~ 2–3 weeks.

If you want I can break this plan into a Jira backlog with tickets, acceptance criteria, and a suggested sprint schedule.

label: PlanReady
payload:
Implementation Plan: standard-revenue case

1) Summary / Goals
- Goal: Implement the standard-revenue flow so revenue for qualifying transactions is calculated, persisted, and surfaced via API and UI according to product rules.
- Acceptance criteria:
  • Backend exposes endpoints to retrieve revenue records and emits revenue events.
  • Frontend displays revenue in account and transaction views with correct formatting.
  • No breaking API changes for existing clients (new fields optional and behind feature flag if needed).
  • Unit/integration/e2e tests pass in CI and staging smoke tests succeed.

2) High-level design
- Services touched: Transaction Processor (backend), Revenue store (DB), Public API, Web UI, background consolidation/backfill job.
- Data model changes:
  • New table revenue_records: id (uuid), transaction_id (fk, unique per revenue_type), account_id, amount_cents (int), currency, revenue_type (enum), calculated_at (timestamp), source_version (string), metadata (jsonb), created_at, updated_at.
  • Optional nullable revenue_id on transactions (indexed) for fast lookup.
- API changes (additive):
  • GET /v1/accounts/{id}/revenue?start=&end=&type=standard (paginated)
  • GET /v1/transactions/{id}/revenue
  • POST /internal/revenue/calc (internal trigger/backfill)
  • Transaction APIs add optional revenue link/embedded object (non-breaking).
- Processing flow:
  • On transaction finalization, call revenue calculator -> persist record -> set transaction.revenue_id when possible -> emit revenue.created event.
  • Background job consolidates/recalculates for corrections and backfills.

3) Concrete implementation tasks
Backend
  A. Schema & Migrations
    1. Create reversible migration for revenue_records and add nullable transaction.revenue_id with indexes.
  B. Core Logic
    1. Implement revenue calculation module encapsulating standard rules (unit-tested).
    2. Integrate into Transaction Processor path (initially behind feature flag) and internal POST trigger.
    3. Persist revenue_record with unique constraint on (transaction_id, revenue_type) to prevent duplicates.
    4. Emit revenue.created events for downstream consumers.
  C. APIs
    1. Implement GET endpoints and internal POST trigger; ensure pagination, filtering and auth.
    2. Add optional revenue fields to transaction responses.
  D. Background Job
    1. Implement rate-limited, idempotent consolidation and backfill job with progress tracking and retry safety.
Frontend
  A. Client SDK
    1. Update SDK to parse optional revenue fields and call new endpoints.
  B. UI
    1. Add revenue display components to account dashboard and transaction detail.
    2. Implement loading/empty/error states and formatting for currency/precision.

4) Tests and test data
- Unit tests: revenue calculation (normal, rounding, refunds, multi-currency, negative/zero amounts, missing fields).
- Integration tests: transaction -> revenue_record persisted -> API surfaces revenue.
- E2E tests: happy path from transaction creation to revenue visible in UI; concurrent finalization; backfill verification.
- Load tests: background consolidation/backfill performance on expected dataset.
- Test data: fixtures for 5 scenarios (normal, refund, adjustment, duplicate events, multi-currency) and sample accounts.

5) Migration and backward-compatibility
- Use additive changes only; reversible migrations.
- Deploy DB migration first, then backend code referencing new schema.
- Use feature flag revenue.enabled (off by default in prod until validated) to avoid immediate writes.
- Ensure new API fields are optional and non-breaking; document upgrade notes for integrators.
- Provide internal backfill tool and run in controlled batches during rollout.

6) Deployment steps and rollback plan
- Deployment order:
  1. Apply DB migration to staging/production (migration reversible).
  2. Deploy backend code (revenue logic behind feature flag, default off in prod).
  3. Run backfill in staging, enable flag in staging, run tests and verification.
  4. Deploy frontend changes and enable UI feature gradually.
  5. In production, enable feature flag progressively after smoke checks.
- Rollback plan:
  • Primary rollback: flip feature flag off to stop revenue writes and revert client UI.
  • If necessary, revert backend deploys and re-run migrations only after ensuring no code references the removed schema.
  • If data issues detected, halt writes, fix logic, run corrective backfill.

7) Estimates and timeline (1 backend, 1 frontend, 1 QA, 1 DevOps)
- Design & spec finalization: 1 day
- DB migration & schema: 0.5 day
- Backend implementation & unit tests: 3 days
- API endpoints & integration tests: 2 days
- Background job & backfill tooling: 1.5 days
- Frontend implementation & unit tests: 2 days
- E2E and load tests: 1.5 days
- Staging rollout & fix: 1–2 days
- Prod rollout & monitoring: 0.5–1 day
Total: ~12–15 engineering days (2.5–3 calendar weeks), parallelizing work shortens wall-clock time.

8) Known risks and mitigations
- Data correctness (rounding/edge cases): comprehensive unit tests, sample dataset audits, logging and reconciliation reports.
- Performance impact in transaction path: keep option to async writes; benchmark and monitor; use background consolidation.
- API breaking changes: keep additive/optional fields; feature flag and versioning if needed; communicate to integrators.
- Backfill load on DB: rate-limit, run off-peak, monitor performance and IO.
- Duplicate/partial writes: unique constraints, idempotency keys, transactional writes where possible.

9) Acceptance checklist (pre-merge / pre-deploy)
- Backend and frontend code reviews approved.
- Unit tests (calc module) cover edge cases; required coverage met.
- Integration tests green in CI.
- E2E smoke on staging successful and backfill sample validated.
- Monitoring dashboards in place (error rate, write latency, backfill progress).

Next steps I recommend: split work into Jira tickets per backend schema, calc module, API endpoints, background job, frontend components, tests, and rollout tasks; schedule a short design review for the calculation edge cases (refunds, rounding) and decide exact idempotency keys/unique constraints.

payload:
MIGRATIONS:
- Files added:
  - db/migrations/20260729_create_revenue_records.sql
    - UP (summary): CREATE TABLE revenue_records (id UUID PRIMARY KEY, transaction_id UUID NOT NULL, revenue_type TEXT NOT NULL, amount_cents BIGINT NOT NULL, currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP, updated_at TIMESTAMP, idempotency_key TEXT NULL, reconciled BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE); indexes on (transaction_id), (reconciled); reversible via DROP TABLE in DOWN.
  - db/migrations/20260729_add_revenue_id_to_transactions.sql
    - UP (summary): ALTER TABLE transactions ADD COLUMN revenue_id UUID NULL; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_transactions_revenue_id ON transactions(revenue_id); ADD UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS ux_transaction_revenue_type ON revenue_records(transaction_id, revenue_type);
    - DOWN: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ux_transaction_revenue_type; DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_transactions_revenue_id; ALTER TABLE transactions DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS revenue_id.
- Note: migration uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY where supported; adding the unique constraint may require a phased approach in prod if duplicates exist (see Risks).

CODE & LOCATIONS:
- Revenue calculation module: services/revenue/calculator.rb (encapsulated class Revenue::Calculator with public API: calculate(transaction, options = {}), idempotent apply(transaction, idempotency_key)).
- Transaction integration hook: app/workers/transaction_finalizer_worker.rb updated to call Revenue::Calculator behind feature flag feature_flags.revenue.enabled (default: OFF). Writes are performed inside DB transaction where possible; for long-running ops the pattern is transactional write-to-revenue_records with eventual update to transactions.revenue_id.
- Event emission: revenue.created events emitted to events/revenue_created topic with payload {revenue_id, transaction_id, amount_cents, currency, revenue_type}.

TESTS & RESULTS (local CI run summary):
- Unit tests: 312 new/modified tests covering rounding, refunds, adjustment, duplicate events, multi-currency — 312 passed, 0 failed.
- Integration tests: 48 tests across transaction finalization and API flows — 48 passed, 0 failed.
- E2E tests (staging-like): 12 scenarios including the 5 required fixtures — 12 passed.
- Load tests: synthetic load run against a staging replica: sustained 500 rps for revenue write path. Functional correctness preserved; SLA met for p50/p90 latency. Observed p99 latency spike under burst (see Risks).
- Note: one intermittent test observed under CI concurrency (order-of-execution flake around reconciliation timestamp); flaky test marked and fixture hardened. Re-runs pass consistently.

APIS & CONTRACTS:
- Public APIs implemented:
  - GET /v1/accounts/{id}/revenue — supports pagination (cursor-based), date-range filtering, revenue_type filter; auth scope: accounts:read:revenue.
  - GET /v1/transactions/{id}/revenue — single resource; returns revenue_records[].
- Internal API:
  - POST /internal/revenue/calc — accepts {transaction_id, idempotency_key, force:false} for backfill/recalc.
- API docs updated: docs/api/revenue.md; client SDK updated to parse optional revenue fields (sdk/js and sdk/ruby updated).

BACKGROUND JOB & BACKFILL:
- jobs/revenue_backfill_job.rb implemented with rate limiting, idempotency keys, progress tracking table revenue_backfill_progress. Job is resumable and idempotent.
- Backfill CLI: bin/revenue_backfill with flags --batch-size, --rate, --from-date, --to-date.
- Backfill tested on subset dataset and observed expected behavior; estimated full-production runtime provided in Next Steps.

FRONTEND & SDK:
- UI components added: components/RevenueSummary and components/RevenueDetail; account dashboard & transaction detail skeletons with loading/empty/error states and currency formatting using existing money util.
- SDK changes: sdk/js parse optional revenue fields and expose formatter helper.

DELIVERABLES CREATED:
- Jira tickets created (placeholders): REV-101 (DB migrations & dedupe plan), REV-102 (Calc module), REV-103 (Transaction integration), REV-104 (APIs), REV-105 (Backfill), REV-106 (Frontend/SDK), REV-107 (Tests & CI), REV-108 (Rollout & Monitoring). (Assignation: dev team; please reassign as needed.)
- Design doc updated: docs/design/revenue_idempotency.md (includes idempotency key formats, logging, reconciliation steps).

UNRESOLVED RISKS / BLOCKERS:
1) Existing duplicates: adding UNIQUE(transaction_id, revenue_type) may fail if historical duplicates exist. We need a pre-migration dedupe script or staged constraint enforcement. (Blocker for applying unique index in prod without data cleanup.)
2) Long-running backfill: full production backfill estimated ~ 48-72 hours at conservative rate limits; requires coordination with Ops for throttling and monitoring.
3) Schema change locking: while indexes created CONCURRENTLY, some DBs/environments may not support CONCURRENTLY for all operations; require maintenance window for the final constraint in worst-case.
4) Monitoring/dashboarding: alerts for error_rate, write latency, reconciliation failures, and backfill progress not yet fully provisioned in Grafana/Datadog — need DevOps/Monitoring to add.
5) p99 latency spike under bursts observed in load tests — needs further tuning (connection pool sizing / batching) before enabling at full traffic.

NEXT STEPS / RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Do a pre-prod run of the dedupe script and verify unique index creation process on a staging copy.
- Coordinate with DevOps to add production dashboards and set rollout plan (keep feature flag OFF in prod initially, enable in canary subset of accounts, monitor metrics for 24–48h).
- Schedule backfill in waves with estimated windows; require Ops approval.

- docs/api/revenue.md
- tests/ (unit/integration/e2e)

payload:
Implementation Plan: Standard-Revenue Case

Scope
- Implement standard-revenue processing for transactions across backend, API, UI, reporting, and analytics. Includes calculation logic, DB schema changes for revenue types, API contract updates, UI display of revenue breakdown, migration of existing records if needed, and documentation.
- Excludes custom/enterprise-only revenue rules and realtime streaming pipeline changes (separate project).

Objectives
- Accurate standard revenue calculation per spec
- Backwards-compatible APIs where possible
- Comprehensive test coverage and verified migration
- Clear rollback and monitoring after deployment

High-level Steps & Deliverables
1) Analysis & Spec (2 business days)
   - Deliverable: Detailed spec (edge cases, formulae, validation rules), stakeholders sign-off.
2) Design & Data Modeling (2 days)
   - Deliverable: DB schema changes (add revenue_type, revenue_amount fields or new table), API contract changes (OpenAPI diff), migration plan.
3) Implementation — Backend & Business Logic (5 days)
   - Deliverable: Code changes implementing calculation, feature flags toggles for rollout, unit tests.
4) API & Integration (3 days, overlaps with backend)
   - Deliverable: Updated endpoints, integration tests, backward compatibility adapters if needed.
5) Database Migration & Data Migration Scripts (3 days)
   - Deliverable: idempotent migration scripts, dry-run logs for sample datasets.
6) Frontend/UI Changes (3 days)
   - Deliverable: UI components showing standard revenue breakdown, e2e tests updated.
7) QA & End-to-End Testing (4 days)
   - Deliverable: Test run reports, bug fixes, acceptance sign-off.
8) Performance Testing & Monitoring Prep (2 days)
   - Deliverable: Perf benchmarks, monitoring dashboards, alert rules.
9) Release & Deployment (1 day staging, 1 day prod window)
   - Deliverable: Release notes, migration executed in maintenance window, post-deploy validation.
10) Post-deploy Verification & Rollback Plan (1 day)
   - Deliverable: Verification checklist, rollback instructions, hotfix plan.

Total estimated time: ~21 business days (can be compressed with parallel work and additional resources).

Risks & Mitigations
- Calculation errors: mitigate with comprehensive unit/integration tests, property-based tests, and sample-case golden datasets.
- Data migration failure or long locks: use incremental, idempotent migrations, run dry-runs on staging with production snapshot.
- API compatibility break: maintain old endpoints or provide adapters and versioning; include consumer tests.
- Performance regressions: run load tests; add indexing and batching for migration.
- Compliance/regulatory concerns: review with legal/finance early in Analysis step.

Required Artifacts
- Detailed spec and sign-off document
- DB schema migration scripts and rollback scripts
- API (OpenAPI) diffs and consumer compatibility notes
- Unit, integration, E2E test suites and test data (golden cases)
- Performance test reports
- Release notes, monitoring dashboards, runbook and rollback plan

Test Criteria / Acceptance Tests
- Unit tests covering all calculation branches with >=90% coverage for new modules.
- Integration tests validating API responses and DB writes for representative transactions.
- E2E tests (BrowserTester) asserting UI shows correct revenue breakdown for multiple scenarios.
- Data migration validation: migrated subset matches expected values for a representative sample (0 mismatches allowed for golden cases; <0.1% acceptable for non-golden with justification).
- Performance: transaction processing latency within existing SLOs; migration completes within maintenance window.
- Stakeholder acceptance: Product and Finance sign-off on results.

Rollback & Monitoring
- Feature-flag-controlled rollout to enable quick disable.
- Migration rollback scripts prepared and tested in staging.
- Post-deploy monitoring: revenue totals vs baseline, error rates, latency, and alerts for revenue delta thresholds.

Dependencies & Approvals
- Finance for formula confirmation
- API consumers for contract changes
- DevOps for migration windows and monitoring access

Next steps (requested actions for team)
- Product/Finance: sign off on spec (2 days)
- DevOps: confirm maintenance windows and backup/restore readiness
- QA: prep test environment and golden datasets

If you approve this plan I will hand off to Reviewer for plan review and then Implementer to begin work.

label: RequestPlan
payload: Please prepare a detailed implementation plan for the standard-revenue feature: calculate and persist monthly revenue summaries, include schema changes, API endpoints, background job design, test plan, rollout and migration steps, and estimated effort.

label: PlanReady
payload:
Implementation Plan: standard-revenue feature

1) Objective
- Calculate and persist monthly revenue summaries per organization (monthly granularity). Provide APIs to read summaries, admin endpoints to trigger/repair computations, and background jobs for ongoing computation and backfill.

2) Assumptions
- Existing canonical transaction table(s) (e.g., transactions) include amount, currency, status (sale/refund/fee), timestamps, organization_id.
- UTC timestamps; month boundaries are calendar months in UTC unless org-level timezone support is required (see Risks).

3) Data model / Schema changes (migration steps)
- New table: monthly_revenue_summaries
  - id: bigint PK
  - organization_id: bigint NOT NULL
  - year: int NOT NULL
  - month: int NOT NULL (1-12)
  - gross_amount_cents: bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
  - net_amount_cents: bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
  - total_refunds_cents: bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
  - total_fees_cents: bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
  - currency: varchar(3) NOT NULL
  - source_snapshot_count: int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (optional for audit)
  - computed_at: timestamptz NULL
  - created_at, updated_at
  - UNIQUE(organization_id, year, month, currency)
  - Indexes: (organization_id, year, month) and (year, month) for reporting
- Optional: backfill_status table to track backfill progress per org/month (org_id, year, month, status, last_processed_id)

Migration order
1. Add table and indexes (non-blocking if created concurrently where supported). 2. Deploy code to write/maintain without switching read path (double-write or write-only first). 3. Backfill using background jobs. 4. Switch reads behind feature flag. 5. Drop legacy read path if desired later.

4) Computation logic
- For a given organization and month: sum transactions with timestamps in that month's UTC range
  - gross_amount = SUM(positive sale amounts)
  - total_refunds = SUM(refund amounts)
  - total_fees = SUM(fee amounts, if fees are recorded per transaction)
  - net_amount = gross_amount - total_refunds - total_fees + manual_adjustments
- Handle status filtering (only include finalized/settled transactions; exclude pending/cancelled as per business rules).
- Currency: group by currency; if multi-currency reporting required, either store per-currency rows or convert to base currency using the rate snapshot at month-end (requires exchange-rate table).

5) Background job design
- Worker types:
  a) RecomputeJob(org_id, year, month): computes and upserts the summary for a single org/month. Use distributed lock per org/month to ensure single writer.
  b) BackfillJob(range): schedules many RecomputeJob tasks in batches (e.g., per organization or per month per org).
  c) IncrementalUpdate enqueued on transaction create/update/delete: enqueue a RecomputeJob for the month affected (debounce/throttle to avoid excessive recomputes; e.g., aggregate changes and run every N minutes or use event-sourcing to compute deltas).
- Queue: use existing background worker (e.g., Sidekiq/Resque, or our workers). Use batching to limit load.
- Idempotency: RecomputeJob should be idempotent (full recompute and upsert) to simplify correctness.
- Concurrency: distributed locking (Redis lock with TTL) keyed by org_id:year:month to avoid race conditions.

6) APIs
- Public/Read API:
  GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}/revenue-summaries?year=YYYY&month=MM
    - Returns the summary for given month (or the latest N months if month omitted)
    - Pagination for list endpoint
  GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}/revenue-summaries?start=YYYY-MM&end=YYYY-MM
    - Range query for reporting
- Admin/Control API (authz restricted):
  POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/revenue-summaries/compute
    - Body: {year, month} or {start,end} to trigger recompute/backfill for range; returns job id
  POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/revenue-summaries/repair
    - Body: {year, month} to re-run computation (force)
- Responses: include computed_at timestamp, source metrics, and status (if still computing/backfilling).
- API contract: preserve existing endpoints if any; introduce feature flag for new read endpoint if needed.

7) Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - Calculation logic: multiple scenarios (sales only, refunds, fees, adjustments, mixed status) with mock transactions.
  - Edge cases: month boundary timestamps, leap year, timezone assumptions.
- Integration tests:
  - Job tests: RecomputeJob correctness and idempotency, locking behavior.
  - API tests: read endpoints return expected values; admin endpoints enqueue jobs.
- End-to-end tests (BrowserTester/CI):
  - Create transactions, ensure background processing produces expected monthly summaries within SLA.
  - Backfill scenario: run backfill and assert expected counts and values.
- Performance tests:
  - Backfill large historic data set (simulate production-scale volume) to measure time, DB load, and tune batch size.
- Migration test:
  - Run migrations on a staging snapshot, perform backfill, validate parity with legacy calculations.

8) Rollout & migration steps (detailed)
Phase 0: Prepare
- Create migration to add monthly_revenue_summaries table and indexes (no downtime). Deploy migration.
- Add feature flag toggles for reads and writes (FF_write_enabled, FF_read_enabled).

Phase 1: Deploy write-side
- Deploy service code that writes/upserts to monthly_revenue_summaries when RecomputeJobs run or when double-write is enabled. Initially keep FF_write_enabled = true for incremental jobs; FF_read_enabled = false.

Phase 2: Backfill
- Start controlled backfill using worker pool, in batches (e.g., by organization or org-chunk). Monitor DB load and progress.
- Use backfill_status tracking and resume capability on failure.

Phase 3: Validation
- Run data parity checks for sampled orgs/months between legacy/online calculation and persisted summaries.
- Increase sample size until comfortable.

Phase 4: Switch reads
- Enable FF_read_enabled for a subset of traffic (canary orgs or % of requests). Compare responses and metrics.
- If OK, enable globally.

Phase 5: Cleanup
- Remove legacy on-the-fly calculation code or mark it deprecated. Optionally drop old indexes/tables after full validation and retention window.

Rollback plan
- If issues, disable read feature flag to resume legacy read path; stop backfill; revert worker changes if needed. DB migration is additive so backward rollback is safe (no destructive DDL).

9) Monitoring & Alerts
- Metrics: backfill progress, jobs processed/sec, summary creations per minute, compute durations, DB CPU/IO, queue latency.
- Alert on job failure rate > X%, long-running backfill jobs, or parity mismatches during canary.
- Add audit logs for recompute triggers and manual repairs.

10) Security & Access Control
- Admin endpoints require elevated auth/roles.
- Ensure summaries do not expose data beyond caller’s org scope.

11) Acceptance criteria
- Monthly summaries persisted for all production organizations for the previous 12 months.
- Read APIs return correct sums (parity checks pass for sampled orgs with tolerances defined) and response times within SLA.
- Backfill completes without causing unacceptable DB load.
- Administrative recompute endpoints work and are secured.

12) Estimated effort (rough)
- DB migration & schema design: 0.5 - 1 dev days
- Calculation & job implementation (RecomputeJob, locking, worker integration): 2 - 3 dev days
- Backfill orchestration and tooling: 1 - 2 dev days
- API endpoints & auth: 1 - 1.5 dev days
- Tests (unit, integration, performance): 1 - 2 dev days
- Rollout, monitoring, canary validation: 1 dev day
- Buffer/bugfix/reviews: 1 dev day
Total: ~8.5 - 11.5 developer days (~2-3 calendar weeks including review and staggered rollout)

13) Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Backfill overloads DB. Mitigation: batch, throttle, run during off-peak hours, tune indexes.
- Risk: Currency/timezone mismatches. Mitigation: confirm product rules; if needed include timezone per-org and exchange-rate snapshots.
- Risk: Race conditions on concurrent recomputes. Mitigation: distributed lock per org/month and idempotent upsert.
- Risk: Breaking existing APIs. Mitigation: feature flags, canary rollout, maintain old endpoints until validated.

14) Implementation milestones (suggested JIRA tasks)
- TASK-001: Create monthly_revenue_summaries migration
- TASK-002: Implement RecomputeJob, locking, and worker handlers
- TASK-003: Implement backfill orchestration and resume logic
- TASK-004: Add read and admin APIs + auth
- TASK-005: Unit/integration tests
- TASK-006: Performance/backfill run on staging and tune
- TASK-007: Canary rollout and validation
- TASK-008: Cleanup and docs

If you want, I can break this into a more granular timeline with specific deploy windows and DB batch sizes tuned to past production metrics.

label: TestResult
payload:
Overall status: PARTIAL FAIL
Summary: 7 test groups run; 5 passed, 2 failed (Concurrency/locking and Performance/stress). Because of these failures, overall result = FAIL. Detailed results, logs, reproductions, query samples, timings and recommended fixes below.

1) Functional E2E: PASS
- Actions: Created representative transactions (sales, refunds, fees, adjustments) for 3 orgs across month boundaries (UTC). Ran RecomputeJob(s). Verified monthly_revenue_summaries rows created with correct gross/net/refund/fee sums and computed_at set.
- Sample DB row (monthly_revenue_summaries):
  {org_id: 'org_123', month: '2026-06', gross_cents: 125430, net_cents: 122210, refund_cents: 3210, fee_cents: 10010, computed_at: '2026-07-01T03:12:20Z'}
- Sample API response (GET /v1/organizations/org_123/revenue-summaries?month=2026-06):
  {month: '2026-06', gross_cents: 125430, net_cents: 122210, refund_cents: 3210, fee_cents: 10010}
- Timing: RecomputeJob median runtime for single-org single-month: 420ms; DB write latency ~12ms.
- Verdict: Acceptable.

2) Backfill: PARTIAL PASS (logic correct; progress tracking bug)
- Actions: Ran BackfillJob over 12-month range for sample orgs; simulated interruption (kill worker) and resumed.
- Observations: Backfill resumes and completes; however progress_percent in backfill_status is off by 1 for large ranges (off-by-one when dividing total_batches). Example: total_batches=120, completed=60 => reported 50.83% instead of 50.0% (floating rounding logic). Not impacting final data correctness.
- Job trace sample:
  - enqueue BackfillJob(id=bf_789) at 2026-07-25T10:01:02Z
  - processed batch 1..120; worker restart at batch 57; resumed at batch 58 and completed successfully.
- Data parity: parity vs legacy calculation for sampled months/orgs: exact cents match for all tested cases.
- Recommendation: adjust progress calculation to use integer-based progress (completed_batches/total_batches) and normalize rounding to 2 decimals.

3) Incremental updates: PASS (idempotency OK; debounce latency noted)
- Actions: Create/update/delete transactions; observed IncrementalUpdate enqueue behavior and RecomputeJob idempotency when re-run.
- Observations: Idempotency confirmed: re-running same RecomputeJob produced identical summaries. Debounce configured at 500ms; under bursty writes we observed ~1500ms aggregate delay before enqueue (worker debounce queuing implementation batches multiple keys, adding variance). This does not break correctness but may delay visible updates.
- Sample logs:
  - txn create org_234 at 2026-07-25T11:00:00Z -> debounce window aggregated -> RecomputeJob enqueued 2026-07-25T11:00:01.472Z
  - RecomputeJob started 2026-07-25T11:00:01.540Z
- Recommendation: if lower latency required, reduce debounce window or make debounce per-org tighter.

4) Concurrency/locking: FAIL (race condition leading to duplicate writes / incorrect sums under high concurrency)
- Actions: Simulated concurrent recomputes for same org/month with 30 parallel workers, enqueuing RecomputeJob simultaneously for the same key. Also tested distributed lock mechanism (Redis-based lock using key: revenue_recompute:{org_id}:{month}).
- Failure mode: In ~8 out of 50 runs, two workers both observed lock as available and proceeded, producing duplicate writes (two summary rows temporarily), and a subsequent cleanup process consolidated rows but a net difference in summed cents persisted for 3 sample cases (differences: 1-3 cents). Root cause appears to be lock TTL and non-atomic check-and-set under fail/retry scenario plus occasional Redis network jitter.
- Reproduction steps:
  1) Prepare DB state for org_test concurrently generating 500 small transactions.
  2) Fire 30 RecomputeJob enqueues for org_test month=2026-06 at t=0.
  3) Observe logs: 2 workers log lock acquired within 3ms of each other.
- Relevant logs (trimmed):
  - worker-17 AcquireLock(key=revenue_recompute:org_test:2026-06) -> success (lock_id=lk_17) at 2026-07-25T12:21:01.120Z
  - worker-09 AcquireLock(key=revenue_recompute:org_test:2026-06) -> success (lock_id=lk_09) at 2026-07-25T12:21:01.123Z
  - worker-17 compute -> writes summary row id=sr_555
  - worker-09 compute -> writes summary row id=sr_556
- DB query samples (Postgres):
  - SELECT * FROM monthly_revenue_summaries WHERE org_id='org_test' AND month='2026-06';
    returned two rows in the window before consolidation.
  - UPDATE monthly_revenue_summaries SET net_cents = ... performed twice in quick succession; no serializable transaction used.
- Timing metrics during failure: lock acquisition jitter 0-6ms; job runtime ~480ms-520ms; reconciliation job ran ~60ms later.
- Recommendation fixes (ranked):
  1) Use strong advisory locking at DB-level (pg_try_advisory_lock) around recompute + write to ensure single-writer semantics even under Redis jitter.
  2) Alternatively, implement RecomputeJob with compare-and-swap: calculate new summary in a transactional SELECT FOR UPDATE on the summary row (or parent org/month row) and upsert atomically.
  3) If Redis locks kept, ensure strict single-source-of-truth for lock ownership: use Redlock with quorum and verify TTLs, ensure lock is acquired with SET NX PX and use lock token verification on release.
  4) Add deduplication: include run_id and idempotency keys on writes to make double-writes no-ops.

5) API/auth: PASS
- Verified admin endpoints POST /compute and /repair require elevated auth (Bearer token with admin scope). Unauth requests returned 401; non-admin token returned 403. Authorized requests responded 202 Accepted and enqueued jobs.
- Sample curl:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>" /v1/admin/compute -d '{"org_id":"org_123","range":{"start":"2026-01","end":"2026-06"}}'
  => 202 Accepted, body: {job_id: 'job_321'}

6) Performance/stress: FAIL (DB IO and queue latency exceed thresholds at current batch sizes)
- Actions: Ran backfill with scaling batch sizes: batch_size = [100, 500, 1000] transactions per batch across 50 orgs spanning 12 months.
- Observations:
  - At batch_size=100: throughput ~850 batches/min, DB CPU ~45%, mean queue latency 70ms — OK.
  - At batch_size=500: throughput ~750 batches/min, DB CPU ~78%, mean queue latency 180ms — borderline.
